schema.description: Type vocabulary used by every concept in this bundle.
schema.body:
# OKF Type Registry & Bundle Conventions

This schema document registers the open type vocabulary used across all concepts in the MediFlux Open Knowledge Format (OKF) bundle.

## Conventions

- **File Naming**: All files use lowercase kebab-case and end with `.md`. Concepts represent individual topics, guides, and reference entries.
- **Reserved Files**:
  - `index.md`: Present at bundle root and in subdirectories to provide hierarchical listings. Only the root `index.md` contains frontmatter (`okf_version: "0.2"`).
  - `log.md`: Chronological log of bundle updates organized under ISO-8601 date headings (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- **Relationships and Links**:
  - Semantic connections between documents are expressed as standard Markdown links (`/docs/...` or relative links).
  - Frontmatter `related:` lists from legacy MDX are converted to body markdown links under a dedicated `## Related` heading.
- **Update History**:
  - Major lifecycle and bundle history is maintained in [`log.md`](file:///home/mir-mudasir/Desktop/mediflux-docs/okf/log.md).

docs/accounting/accounting-basics.body:
# Accounting Basics

Accounting is the language of business. It is the system of recording, classifying, and summarizing every financial transaction so you understand exactly how your pharmacy is performing. Whether you are tracking daily sales, paying suppliers, or filing GST returns, accounting gives you the clarity to make informed decisions.

> **[Note]** You do not need to be a chartered accountant to use MediFlux. The software automates most entries behind the scenes. This guide exists so you can read your reports with confidence and catch problems early.

## What you will learn

- How the accounting equation keeps your books balanced
- What assets, liabilities, equity, income, and expenses actually mean in a pharmacy
- The golden rules of debit and credit
- How MediFlux structures your Chart of Accounts
- How GST flows through your books
- The difference between profit and cash flow
- How to read your core financial statements

---

## The accounting equation

Every transaction in your pharmacy follows one immovable rule:

**Assets = Liabilities + Equity**

This equation is the foundation of double-entry bookkeeping. Everything your business owns (Assets) is funded either by what you owe to others (Liabilities) or by what belongs to the owners (Equity).

If this equation is ever out of balance, there is an error in your books. Your **Trial Balance** exists specifically to catch this.

---

## The five building blocks

All accounting boils down to five categories. Every account in your Chart of Accounts falls into one of these.

### 1. Assets
---

Assets are things your business owns that have value. MediFlux divides assets into two types based on how quickly they can be converted to cash.

**Current Assets** (convertible to cash within one year):

| Pharmacy Asset | What It Means |
|----------------|---------------|
| **Cash in Hand** | Physical cash in your drawer or safe |
| **Bank Balances** | Money in current, savings, or FD accounts |
| **Drug Inventory** | Value of all medicines in stock |
| **Non-Drug Inventory** | Cosmetics, wellness products, devices |
| **Accounts Receivable** | Money customers owe you for credit sales |
| **Digital Wallets** | UPI, Paytm, or other wallet balances |

**Non-Current Assets** (held for more than one year):

| Pharmacy Asset | What It Means |
|----------------|---------------|
| **Fixed Assets** | Shelves, refrigerators, computers, furniture |

> **[Note]** In MediFlux, **Drug Inventory** and **Non-Drug Inventory** values are calculated automatically from your purchase and sale records.

### 2. Liabilities
---

Liabilities are what your business owes to others. They are grouped by how soon they must be paid.

**Current Liabilities** (due within one year):

| Pharmacy Liability | What It Means |
|--------------------|---------------|
| **Accounts Payable** | Money owed to suppliers for credit purchases |
| **GST Output** | Tax collected from customers, owed to the government |
| **Salary Payable** | Wages due to staff but not yet paid |

**Non-Current Liabilities** (due after one year):

| Pharmacy Liability | What It Means |
|--------------------|---------------|
| **Bank Loans** | Borrowed capital for expansion or working capital |

### 3. Equity
---

Equity is the owner's stake in the business.

| Equity Account | What It Means |
|----------------|---------------|
| **Owner Capital** | Money you or your partners invested |
| **Retained Earnings** | Cumulative profits from previous years, kept in the business |

When you first set up MediFlux Accounting, you enter your **Owner Capital**. The system then calculates **Retained Earnings** automatically to make the equation balance.

### 4. Income (Revenue)
---
Income is money earned from your primary business activities.

- Cash sales at the counter
- Credit sales to customers
- Sales of non-drug items
- Service income (consultations, health checks)

### 5. Expenses
---

Expenses are costs incurred to run the business.

- Purchase of medicines and stock
- Rent, salaries, electricity
- Transportation and courier charges
- Marketing and advertising

> **[Note]** The difference between total income and total expenses is your **Net Profit** or **Net Loss**. This is what your **P&L Statement** shows.

---

## Debit and Credit

Debit and Credit are not simply "plus" and "minus". They are directions. Whether a debit increases or decreases an account depends on the account type.

### The golden rules

| Account Type | Rule | Example |
|--------------|------|---------|
| **Personal** (people, businesses, banks) | Debit the Receiver, Credit the Giver | Paying a supplier: debit Supplier, credit Bank |
| **Real** (assets, stock, cash) | Debit what Comes In, Credit what Goes Out | Buying stock: debit Drug Inventory, credit Bank |
| **Nominal** (income, expenses) | Debit all Expenses and Losses, Credit all Incomes and Gains | Paying rent: debit Rent, credit Bank |

### How debits and credits affect each account type

| Account Type | Debit Means | Credit Means |
|--------------|-------------|--------------|
| **Assets** | Increase | Decrease |
| **Liabilities** | Decrease | Increase |
| **Equity** | Decrease | Increase |
| **Income** | Decrease | Increase |
| **Expenses** | Increase | Decrease |

> **[Warning: Debits and Credits always balance]** Every journal entry must have equal debits and credits. If you debit one account by `₹1,000`, you must credit another account by exactly `₹1,000`. This is why it is called double-entry bookkeeping.

### A simple example

You sell medicines for `₹500` cash:

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Cash on Hand (Asset increases) | `₹500` | |
| Sales Revenue (Income increases) | | `₹500` |

You sell medicines for `₹1,200` on credit to a customer:

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Accounts Receivable (Asset increases) | `₹1,200` | |
| Sales Revenue (Income increases) | | `₹1,200` |

You buy stock worth `₹10,000` on credit from a supplier:

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Drug Inventory (Asset increases) | `₹10,000` | |
| Accounts Payable (Liability increases) | | `₹10,000` |

You buy stock worth `₹5,000` and pay immediately by cash:

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Drug Inventory (Asset increases) | `₹5,000` | |
| Cash on Hand (Asset decreases) | | `₹5,000` |

---

## Ledgers

The **Ledgers** is the master list of every account your pharmacy uses. Think of it as the filing cabinet for your financial data.

MediFlux organizes accounts into **parent groups** and **child accounts**. Parent groups are categories. Child accounts are the actual accounts used in transactions.

### Parent groups

![Parent Account Groups](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/00e5482c-621a-4048-9dce-ed7501ca6b39-parent-accounts.png)
*Caption: The Ledgers showing some parent groups with their types.*

### Assets
| Parent Account | Type | Description |
|----------------|------|-------------|
| **Cash & Bank** | `Current_asset` | All cash, bank, and wallet balances |
| **Accounts Receivable** | `Current_asset` | Amounts customers owe |
| **Inventory** | `Current_asset` | Value of all stock held for sale |
| **Tax Assets** | `Current_asset` | Input GST balances claimable |
| **Prepaid Expenses** | `Current_asset` | Advance payments made |
| **Deposits** | `Non_current_asset` | Refundable deposits paid |
| **Fixed Assets** | `Non_current_asset` | Long-term operational assets |

### Liabilities

| Parent Account | Type | Description |
|----------------|------|-------------|
| **Accounts Payable** | `Current_liability` | Amounts owed to suppliers |
| **GST Payable** | `Current_liability` | GST collected, owed to government |
| **Accrued Expenses** | `Current_liability` | Expenses incurred but not yet paid |
| **Statutory Liabilities** | `Current_liability` | Taxes collected but not remitted |
| **Short-Term Liabilities** | `Current_liability` | Loans due within one year |
| **Long-Term Liabilities** | `Non_current_liability` | Loans due after one year |

### Equity, Revenue, and Expenses

| Parent Account | Type | Description |
|----------------|------|-------------|
| **Equity** | `Equity` | Owner's stake after liabilities |
| **Revenue** | `Revenue` | Income from sales and services |
| **Expenses** | `Expense` | All operating costs |

## Child accounts

Child accounts are the actual accounts used in journal entries. Here is how the **Cash & Bank** parent expands:

![Cash & Bank Child Accounts](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/e208aa82-167e-413f-977d-260860e7d107-cash-and-bank-child-accounts.png)
*Caption: Expanded Cash & Bank parent showing nested child accounts.*

| Child Account | Parent | Description |
|---------------|--------|-------------|
| **Cash on Hand** | Cash & Bank | Physical cash at the store |
| **Bank Accounts** | Cash & Bank | Money held in bank accounts |
| **Test Bank** | Bank Accounts | Individual bank account |
| **Digital Wallets** | Cash & Bank | UPI, wallet, and gateway balances |

Notice that **Bank Accounts** is itself a parent to individual accounts like **Test Bank**. This nested structure lets you see total bank balances at a glance while drilling into specific accounts.

#### Other typical child accounts

**Accounts Receivable**
- **Customer Receivables**: Outstanding credit bills

**Inventory**
- **Drug Inventory**: Medicines and healthcare products
- **Non-Drug Inventory**: Cosmetics and wellness items

**Tax Assets**
- **GST Input CGST**, **GST Input SGST**, **GST Input IGST**

**GST Payable**
- **GST Output CGST**, **GST Output SGST**, **GST Output IGST**

**Equity**
- **Owner Capital**: Investments by owners or partners
- **Retained Earnings**: Auto-calculated historical profits

**Revenue**
- **Sales Revenue**: Drug and non-drug sales
- **Other Income**: Commissions, rental income

**Expenses**
- **Cost of Goods Sold**: Direct inventory cost
- **Rent**, **Salaries**, **Electricity**, **Transportation**

---

## GST in your books

MediFlux is built for Indian pharmacies, so GST is woven into every transaction.

### Output GST (Liability)

Tax you collect from customers and owe to the government.

- **CGST**: Central GST on intra-state sales
- **SGST**: State GST on intra-state sales
- **IGST**: Integrated GST on inter-state sales

### Input GST (Asset)

Tax you pay to suppliers. You claim this as credit against your output liability.

- **GST Input CGST**, **GST Input SGST**, **GST Input IGST**

### Net GST Payable

**Net GST Payable = Output GST - Input GST**

If input exceeds output, the excess carries forward. MediFlux tracks this automatically and supports **ITC Reversals** for returned goods or adjustments.

---

## Cash flow vs Profit

Profit and cash are not the same thing.

- **Profit** is an accounting measure. A credit sale increases profit immediately.
- **Cash** is what you have in the bank. You only receive cash when the customer pays.

You can be profitable on paper but run out of cash if:
- Customers delay payments on credit sales
- You hold too much inventory
- You pay suppliers faster than customers pay you

> **[Note]** A healthy pharmacy needs positive **operating cash flow**. If you are selling stock but constantly short on cash, review your credit terms and inventory purchasing patterns.

---

## Your financial statements

Once your accounts are set up, MediFlux generates three core statements automatically. Each one answers a different question about your business.


  * [Profit & Loss Statement](/docs/accounting/profitandloss-statements.md) - Did I make money this month?
  * [Balance Sheet](/docs/accounting/balance-sheet) - What does my business own and owe right now?
  * [Trial Balance](/docs/accounting/trial-balance) - Do my books actually balance?


# Profit and Loss Statement
---

The **Profit and Loss Statement**, also called the **Income Statement**, tells you whether your pharmacy made or lost money during a specific period. It could be a day, a week, a month, a quarter, or a full financial year.

**Formula**: Revenue - Expenses = Net Profit / Net Loss

### What goes into Revenue

Revenue is the total money earned from selling goods and services before any costs are deducted. In a pharmacy, this includes:

- **Drug Sales**: Income from prescription and over-the-counter medicines
- **Non-Drug Sales**: Income from cosmetics, wellness products, and medical devices
- **Other Income**: Commissions, rental income from clinic space, or service charges

> **[Note]** Revenue includes both cash sales and credit sales. A credit sale counts as revenue even if the customer has not paid yet. This is why profit and cash are different things.

### What goes into Expenses

Expenses are the costs you incur to generate that revenue. They are not the same as buying inventory. Inventory is an asset until it is sold. Expenses include:

- **Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)**: The cost of the medicines and products you actually sold during the period. This is calculated as Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock.
- **Operating Expenses**: Rent, salaries, electricity, transportation, marketing, and other day-to-day costs.
- **Administrative Expenses**: Phone bills, internet, accounting fees, and software subscriptions.
- **Financial Expenses**: Bank charges and interest on loans.

### Gross Profit vs Net Profit

**Gross Profit = Revenue - Cost of Goods Sold**

Gross profit tells you how much you earn from selling stock before considering rent, salaries, and other overheads. A low gross profit means your buying price is too high or your selling price is too low.

**Net Profit = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses - Other Expenses**

Net profit is your bottom line. It is what remains after every cost is deducted. This is the number that matters most for understanding whether your pharmacy is truly profitable.

### Why the P&L matters

- It shows trends: Are your expenses growing faster than your sales?
- It reveals margins: Is your markup enough to cover overheads?
- It guides decisions: Should you discontinue a low-margin product line? Can you afford to hire another staff member?

> **[Warning: A positive net profit does not mean you have cash]** The P&L includes credit sales as revenue and spreads asset costs over time. You can show a profit while struggling to pay suppliers. Always check your **Cash Flow** alongside your P&L.

# Balance Sheet
---

The **Balance Sheet** is a snapshot of your business at a single point in time, usually the last day of a month or financial year. It answers one question: What is my pharmacy worth right now?

**Formula**: Assets = Liabilities + Equity

### Assets on the Balance Sheet

Assets are listed in order of liquidity, meaning how quickly they can be turned into cash.

**Current Assets** (convertible to cash within one year):
- **Cash in Hand**: Physical cash at the store
- **Bank Balances**: Money in all business bank accounts
- **Accounts Receivable**: Money customers owe you
- **Inventory**: Value of unsold stock
- **Tax Assets**: Input GST you can claim back
- **Prepaid Expenses**: Advance payments like insurance premiums

**Non-Current Assets** (held for more than one year):
- **Fixed Assets**: Furniture, refrigerators, computers, shelves
- **Deposits**: Security deposits for shop premises or equipment

### Liabilities on the Balance Sheet

**Current Liabilities** (due within one year):
- **Accounts Payable**: Money you owe suppliers
- **GST Payable**: Tax collected from customers, owed to the government
- **Accrued Expenses**: Bills received but not yet paid
- **Short-Term Loans**: Borrowings due within a year

**Non-Current Liabilities** (due after one year):
- **Long-Term Loans**: Bank loans or borrowings with repayment beyond one year

### Equity on the Balance Sheet

- **Owner Capital**: The money you and your partners originally invested
- **Retained Earnings**: All profits from previous years that were not withdrawn

### Working Capital

**Working Capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities**

Working capital measures your ability to pay short-term bills. A positive number means you have enough liquid assets to cover near-term obligations. A negative number is a warning sign: you may struggle to pay suppliers or staff even if your P&L looks healthy.

### Why the Balance Sheet matters

- It shows financial health: Are you building wealth or accumulating debt?
- It reveals leverage: Are you funding growth with loans or with profits?
- It helps with loans: Banks ask for Balance Sheets before approving credit.
- It tracks owner equity: You can see exactly how much of the business belongs to you.

# Trial Balance
---

The **Trial Balance** is a list of every account in your Chart of Accounts with its current debit or credit balance. It is not a financial statement you share with outsiders, but it is the most important internal check in your bookkeeping.

**Rule**: Total Debits must equal Total Credits.

### What the Trial Balance contains

Every account from your Chart of Accounts appears once, with its balance in either the Debit column or the Credit column:

- **Asset accounts**: Normally have debit balances
- **Liability accounts**: Normally have credit balances
- **Equity accounts**: Normally have credit balances
- **Revenue accounts**: Normally have credit balances
- **Expense accounts**: Normally have debit balances

If you add up every debit balance and every credit balance, the two totals must be identical.

### Why the Trial Balance must balance

Remember the accounting equation: **Assets = Liabilities + Equity**.

In double-entry bookkeeping, every transaction hits two accounts with equal debits and credits. Over thousands of transactions, this balance must hold. The Trial Balance is the checkpoint that proves it.

### What to do if it does not balance

An unbalanced Trial Balance means there is an error somewhere. Common causes include:

- A transaction was entered with only one side (single entry instead of double entry)
- A debit and credit were recorded for unequal amounts
- An account was classified under the wrong type (asset instead of expense)
- A balance was carried forward incorrectly from a previous period
- A rounding error in GST calculations

> **[Warning: Never ignore an unbalanced Trial Balance]** If your Trial Balance does not balance, your P&L and Balance Sheet will be wrong. Find the error before filing GST returns, applying for loans, or sharing reports with your accountant.

### How MediFlux helps

MediFlux generates the Trial Balance automatically from your journal entries. Since most entries are created automatically when you record sales and purchases, the Trial Balance usually stays balanced. If you create manual journal entries, double-check that your debits and credits are equal before saving.

---

## Common mistakes

- **Confusing profit with cash**: A credit sale boosts profit but not your bank balance until payment arrives.
- **Mixing personal and business expenses**: Record personal withdrawals as **Drawings**, not business expenses.
- **Forgetting small cash expenses**: Tea, stationery, and auto fares add up. Record everything.
- **Ignoring GST on purchases**: Enter the full bill amount including GST so input credit calculates correctly.
- **Not reconciling bank accounts**: Match MediFlux balances with bank statements monthly.
- **Misclassifying account types**: Wrong types break your Trial Balance.

---

## FAQs


  ### Do I need to know accounting to use MediFlux?

No. MediFlux automates journal entries when you record sales and purchases. This guide helps you understand the reports, not operate the software.
  ### What is the difference between a journal and a ledger?

A **journal** is the chronological record of all transactions. A **ledger** groups transactions by account. The **Cash on Hand** ledger shows every transaction that affected cash, with a running balance.
  ### Why are there three types of GST?

CGST and SGST split tax equally between Central and State governments for intra-state sales. IGST applies to inter-state sales and is collected by the Central government for later distribution.
  ### What is Retained Earnings?

It is the cumulative profit or loss from previous years kept in the business. MediFlux calculates it automatically as the balancing figure in your equation.
  ### Can I edit automatic journal entries?

No, to preserve data integrity. Create an adjusting entry manually instead, or reverse and re-enter the original transaction.
  ### What is a contra entry?

A transaction affecting only cash and bank accounts, such as depositing cash into your bank. MediFlux handles these automatically.
  ### Why is my bank account nested under Bank Accounts?

MediFlux uses a two-level structure. **Bank Accounts** is the group header. Individual accounts like **Test Bank** are children. This lets you see totals and drill down.


## Next steps


  * Set up Chart of Accounts - Initialize your accounts and enter opening balances.
  * [Daybook](/docs/accounting/daybook) - See how daily transactions flow through your books.
  * [Ledger](/docs/accounting/ledger) - Drill into individual accounts and their running balances.
  * [Trial Balance](/docs/accounting/trial-balance) - Verify your books are balanced before generating reports.

docs/accounting/add-journal-entry.title: Add Journal Entry
docs/accounting/add-journal-entry.description: Create manual pharmacy journal entries in MediFlux. Record debits, credits, and accounting adjustments following the double-entry rule easily.
docs/accounting/add-journal-entry.body:
# Add Journal Entry

The **Add Journal Entry** page lets you record a **manual pharmacy journal entry** in **MediFlux**. Use it for adjustments, transfers, owner drawings, expense allocations, or any other entry that is not automatically generated by sales, purchases, or payments.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Accounting → Add Journal Entry**.

You can also reach this form by clicking **+ Add Journal** on the **Journals** page.

![MediFlux Add Pharmacy Journal Entry Form](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/da184c26-e634-4148-bf71-af33dcb25ed8-add-journal-entry.png)
*Caption: Full form with transaction date, description, journal lines, and Post Journal button for pharmacy accounting in MediFlux.*

---

## Page Overview

| Element | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Transaction Date** | Date of the journal entry (required) |
| **Journal Description / Reference** | Narrative that explains the purpose of the entry (required) |
| **JOURNAL LINES** | Debit and credit rows that make up the entry |
| **+ Add Ledger Row** | Adds another debit or credit line |
| **TOTAL** | Live totals for Debit and Credit columns |
| **Cancel** | Discards the entry and returns to the previous page |
| **+ Post Journal** | Saves and posts the entry to the ledgers |

![MediFlux Journal Entry Page Overview](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/85fd6371-7acd-490e-91ff-3cf09ae1bc63-overview-journa_.png)
*Caption: Overview of Transaction Date, Journal Description, and journal lines in the MediFlux pharmacy accounting module.*

---

## Header Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Transaction Date** | Yes | Defaults to today. Click the calendar icon to change it. |
| **Journal Description / Reference** | Yes | Short narrative for the entry (for example, "Owner capital introduced" or "Office rent for September"). |

![MediFlux Journal Entry Header Fields](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/cf84f208-0f4b-4345-abe4-8dfc7cbf07a0-headerfiles-journal.png)
*Caption: Required Transaction Date and Journal Description fields for creating a pharmacy journal entry in MediFlux.*

---

## Journal Lines

Every journal entry must follow the **double-entry rule**: total debits must equal total credits. The form enforces a minimum of two lines.

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **ACCOUNT NAME** | Select an account from the Chart of Accounts. Start typing to search. |
| **NOTE / MEMO** | Optional line-level note for extra context. |
| **DEBIT** | Amount to debit this account. Enter `0.00` if the line is a credit. |
| **CREDIT** | Amount to credit this account. Enter `0.00` if the line is a debit. |
| **Delete Icon** | Removes the line. |

![MediFlux Journal Lines Table](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/c17e6cd1-e632-43dc-ac8a-d8d7d392ee51-journal-entry.png)
*Caption: Account Name, Note/Memo, Debit, and Credit columns for double-entry bookkeeping in MediFlux pharmacy accounting.*

### Adding More Lines

Click **+ Add Ledger Row** at the bottom of the table to insert an additional debit or credit line.

![MediFlux Add Ledger Row Button](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/fe66e0ca-79e6-48ab-b0c5-6e723bdef93a-add-jedger-row.png)
*Caption: Button to insert an additional debit or credit line for complex pharmacy journal entries in MediFlux.*

### Totals

The **TOTAL** row at the bottom of the table shows the running sum of all Debit amounts and all Credit amounts. Both totals must be equal before you can post the entry.

> **[Note]** The form shows the message **Min. 2 lines required (double-entry rule)** as a reminder that every journal needs at least one debit and one credit.

---

## Posting the Entry

1. Fill in **Transaction Date** and **Journal Description / Reference**.
2. Select an account and enter either a Debit or Credit amount on the first line.
3. Select a different account and enter the balancing amount on the second line.
4. Add more lines if the entry involves more than two accounts.
5. Confirm that the Debit and Credit totals are equal.
6. Click **+ Post Journal**.

Once posted, the entry appears in:

- **Journals** with type **MANUAL** and status **POSTED**
- **Daybook** under the selected date
- The individual **Ledger** of every account used in the entry

![MediFlux Post Journal Entry Buttons](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/8e8bb749-fe9c-43db-b3fb-fa608bbce95d-cancel-journal.png)
*Caption: Cancel discards the entry, while Post Journal saves and posts the manual pharmacy journal entry to the ledgers in MediFlux.*

---

## Example

A simple transfer of ₹5,000 from Cash to a Bank account:

| Account Name | Note / Memo | Debit | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bank Account – HDFC | September transfer | `5000.00` | `0.00` |
| Cash in Hand | September transfer | `0.00` | `5000.00` |

Totals: Debit `₹5,000.00` = Credit `₹5,000.00`

---

## Common Mistakes

> **[Warning: Debits do not equal credits]** The form will not allow you to post an unbalanced entry. Always check the **TOTAL** row before clicking **Post Journal**.

> **[Warning: Leaving the description blank]** **Journal Description / Reference** is required. A clear narrative makes the entry easy to understand later in the Daybook and Journals list.

---

## After Posting


  * [Journals](/docs/accounting/journals) - View the entry you just posted along with all other journals.
  * [Daybook](/docs/accounting/daybook) - See the new entry in the chronological transaction list.
  * [General Ledger](/docs/accounting/general-ledger) - Open any account used in the entry to see its running balance.
  * [Trial Balance](/docs/accounting/trial-balance) - Confirm that total debits still equal total credits across all accounts.

docs/accounting/balance-sheet.title: Balance Sheet
docs/accounting/balance-sheet.description: View your pharmacy balance sheet in MediFlux. Track assets, liabilities, and equity to understand your business's financial position easily.
docs/accounting/balance-sheet.body:
# Balance Sheet

The **Balance Sheet** is a snapshot of your **pharmacy's financial position** at a single point in time in **MediFlux**. It answers one fundamental question: what does the business own, and how is it financed? The sheet is divided into three sections: **Assets**, **Liabilities**, and **Equity**. It is governed by the accounting equation:

**Assets = Liabilities + Equity**

In MediFlux, the Balance Sheet is generated automatically from your ledger balances. Unlike the Trial Balance, which lists every account with its activity, the Balance Sheet groups accounts into meaningful categories and shows only the net closing balance of each.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Accounting → Balance Sheet**.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Balance Sheet Overview](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/6db518d3-55d9-41e0-9003-61d9a8be46ef-BS-OVERVIEW.png)
*Caption: A snapshot of a pharmacy's financial position on a selected date, showing Assets, Liabilities, and Equity in MediFlux.*

---

## Search and Filter by Date

The Balance Sheet is a snapshot, not a period report. Use the date picker at the top to select the **as-on date**. This defaults to today. Click the field to open the calendar and pick any past date to see what your financial position looked like then.

Use **Search ledgers** to find a specific account by name instantly.

![MediFlux Balance Sheet Search and Date Filter](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/0cc13cc3-18d8-4613-b80b-9836f28225ea-search-bs.png)
*Caption: Select any past date to view the pharmacy financial position as on that specific day in MediFlux.*

---

## Summary Cards

Four cards sit at the top, giving you the big picture at a glance:

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Total Assets** | The total value of everything the business owns. Shown as a debit balance |
| **Total Liabilities** | The total amount the business owes to others. Shown as a credit balance |
| **Total Equity** | The owner's stake in the business. Shown as a credit balance |
| **Current Year Earnings** | The net profit or loss accumulated in the current accounting period, not yet closed to Retained Earnings |

![MediFlux Balance Sheet Summary Cards](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/c77bad36-cf66-4934-8397-f59b28742f41-bs-summaryCards.png)
*Caption: Summary cards showing Total Assets, Total Liabilities, Total Equity, and Current Year Earnings for a pharmacy.*

> **[Note]** **Total Assets** must always equal **Total Liabilities + Total Equity**. If these numbers do not match, there is a fundamental error in the books that must be resolved.

---

## Assets

Assets are what your pharmacy owns. They are listed in order of liquidity, with the most liquid assets (cash, receivables) at the top and fixed assets at the bottom.

| Column | What it means |
|--------|---------------|
| **Ledger** | Account name with `Dr` or `Cr` badge. Parent groups can be expanded to reveal child accounts |
| **Balance** | The net closing balance of the account or group. Shown as `Dr` for assets |

Click the arrow next to any parent group to expand it and see the individual child account balances.

### Example: Newly Initialized Store

![MediFlux Newly Initialized Store Balance Sheet](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/881645eb-4973-4ab8-a0bb-43afbe8c12d8-new-acc-bs.png)
*Caption: Minimal but balanced Balance Sheet for a newly initialized pharmacy store in MediFlux, showing only inventory and tax assets.*

| Account | Balance |
|---------|---------|
| **Inventory** | `₹23,420.02 Dr` |
| Medicine Inventory | `₹16,495.02 Dr` |
| Non-Drug Inventory | `₹6,925.00 Dr` |
| **Tax Assets** | `₹1,196.90 Dr` |
| GST Input CGST | `₹598.45 Dr` |
| GST Input SGST | `₹598.45 Dr` |
| **Total Assets** | `₹24,616.92 Dr` |

In this example, the store has just been initialized. The only assets are inventory stock and input GST credits. There are no bank balances, receivables, or fixed assets yet.

### Example: Mature Store

![MediFlux Mature Pharmacy Store Assets Section](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/04727d2d-c4cc-42ed-95f3-a84b30ce3084-mature-store-bs.png)
*Caption: Assets section of a mature pharmacy store Balance Sheet with Cash & Bank, Receivables, Inventory, and Tax Assets fully expanded.*

| Account | Balance |
|---------|---------|
| **Cash & Bank** | `₹47,30,287.80 Dr` |
| Cash on Hand | `₹3,45,316.80 Dr` |
| Bank Accounts | `₹43,61,971.00 Dr` |
| **Accounts Receivable** | `₹94,581.31 Dr` |
| Customer Receivables | `₹94,581.31 Dr` |
| **Inventory** | `₹11,07,865.75 Dr` |
| Medicine Inventory | `₹10,74,632.27 Dr` |
| Non-Drug Inventory | `₹37,414.07 Dr` |
| Purchase Return | `₹3,902.99 Cr` |
| Purchase Return - Non-Drug Inventory | `₹77.70 Cr` |
| **Tax Assets** | `₹2,61,042.70 Dr` |
| GST Input CGST | `₹1,12,307.96 Dr` |
| GST Input SGST | `₹1,47,324.84 Dr` |
| GST Input IGST | `₹1,408.80 Dr` |
| **Total Assets** | `₹61,93,777.56 Dr` |

> **[Note]** **Purchase Return** and **Purchase Return - Non-Drug Inventory** carry credit balances. These are **contra-asset** accounts that reduce the total value of inventory.

---

## Liabilities

Liabilities are what your pharmacy owes to others. They are listed in order of due date, with current liabilities (due within a year) first.

### Example: Newly Initialized Store

| Account | Balance |
|---------|---------|
| **Accounts Payable** | `₹9,984.00 Cr` |
| Trade Creditors | `₹9,984.00 Cr` |
| **Total Liabilities** | `₹9,984.00 Cr` |

### Example: Mature Store

![MediFlux Pharmacy Liabilities Section](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/17fff84e-2586-43a8-842f-faf40a4c38a6-liabilities-bs.png)
*Caption: Liabilities section of a mature pharmacy store Balance Sheet showing Accounts Payable and GST Payable with sub-accounts.*

| Account | Balance |
|---------|---------|
| **Accounts Payable** | `₹3,00,699.63 Cr` |
| Trade Creditors | `₹3,00,699.63 Cr` |
| **GST Payable** | `₹26,457.45 Cr` |
| Output GST | `₹26,457.45 Cr` |
| GST Output CGST | `₹12,435.38 Cr` |
| GST Output SGST | `₹12,435.38 Cr` |
| GST Output IGST | `₹1,588.00 Cr` |
| **Total Liabilities** | `₹3,27,157.08 Cr` |

> **[Note]** **GST Payable** is a liability because it represents tax collected from customers that must be remitted to the government.

---

## Equity

Equity represents the owner's residual claim on the assets after all liabilities are settled. It includes capital invested, retained profits from previous years, and the current year's earnings.

### Example: Newly Initialized Store

| Account | Balance |
|---------|---------|
| **Equity** | `₹14,632.92 Cr` |
| Retained Earnings | `₹14,632.92 Cr` |
| **Total Equity** | `₹14,632.92 Cr` |

### Example: Mature Store

![MediFlux Pharmacy Equity Section](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/82fa5fb9-7ea8-497c-bb21-8e460f6c7dec-equity-bs.png)
*Caption: Equity section of a mature pharmacy store Balance Sheet showing Retained Earnings, Current Year Earnings, and owner capital/drawings.*

| Account | Balance |
|---------|---------|
| **Equity** | `₹58,66,620.48 Cr` |
| Retained Earnings | `₹58,13,622.02 Cr` |
| Current Year Earnings (Calculated) | `₹23,651.39 Cr` |
| Mehreen | `₹20,25,594.40 Cr` |
| Owner's Capital - Mehreen | `₹20,26,368.20 Cr` |
| Owner's Drawings - Mehreen | `₹773.80 Dr` |
| **Total Equity** | `₹58,66,620.48 Cr` |

> **[Note]** **Current Year Earnings (Calculated)** is kept separate from **Retained Earnings** so you can see how much the business has earned in the current period. **Owner's Drawings** is a contra-equity account that reduces total equity.

---

## Why Assets Must Equal Liabilities + Equity

Every transaction affects at least two accounts in a way that keeps the accounting equation balanced.

| Transaction | Effect on the equation |
|-------------|------------------------|
| **Owner invests cash** | Assets (Cash) increase, Equity (Capital) increases |
| **Buy inventory on credit** | Assets (Inventory) increase, Liabilities (Accounts Payable) increase |
| **Make a credit sale** | Assets (Accounts Receivable) increase, Equity increases via Revenue |
| **Pay a supplier** | Assets (Cash) decrease, Liabilities (Accounts Payable) decrease |
| **Owner takes drawings** | Assets (Cash) decrease, Equity decreases via Drawings |

Because every transaction maintains the balance, the totals at the bottom of the sheet must always match:

**Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity**

---

## Current vs. Non-Current

The Balance Sheet separates assets and liabilities into **Current** and **Non-Current** categories.

| Category | Definition | Examples |
|----------|------------|----------|
| **Current Assets** | Convertible to cash or used up within one year | Cash, Inventory, Receivables, Prepaid Expenses, Tax Assets |
| **Non-Current Assets** | Held for more than one year | Fixed Assets, Deposits, Equipment, Property |
| **Current Liabilities** | Due for payment within one year | Accounts Payable, GST Payable, Short-Term Loans, Accrued Expenses |
| **Non-Current Liabilities** | Due after more than one year | Long-Term Loans, Mortgage |

This split helps you assess the short-term financial health of the pharmacy.

---

## Common Mistakes

> **[Warning: Thinking the Balance Sheet shows your profit]** The Balance Sheet shows **position**, not **performance**. It tells you what you own and owe on a specific date, not how much you earned during the period. For revenue, expenses, and net profit, open the **Profit and Loss Statement**.

> **[Warning: Ignoring contra accounts that reduce parent totals]** Accounts like **Purchase Return** under Inventory and **Owner's Drawings** under Equity carry opposite balances and actively subtract from their parent group. Always expand parent groups to see the full breakdown.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions


  ### What is the difference between Balance Sheet and Trial Balance?

The **Trial Balance** is an internal tool that lists every ledger with its opening balance, period activity, and closing balance. It is used to verify that debits equal credits. The **Balance Sheet** is a formal financial statement that groups accounts into Assets, Liabilities, and Equity to show the financial position at a point in time.
  ### Why is Current Year Earnings shown separately?

**Current Year Earnings** is a temporary equity account that accumulates net profit or loss from the start of the financial year. It is kept separate from **Retained Earnings** so you can see how much the business has earned in the current period. At year-end, this balance is transferred to Retained Earnings.
  ### Can a liability account show a debit balance?

Normally no, but it can happen in rare cases such as overpayment to a supplier. If a liability account shows a debit balance, it effectively becomes an asset (the supplier owes you money).
  ### Why does Purchase Return appear under Assets?

**Purchase Return** is a **contra-asset** account. It sits under the Inventory parent group but carries a credit balance. It reduces the total value of inventory on the Balance Sheet.
  ### How often should I review the Balance Sheet?

Most pharmacy owners review the Balance Sheet monthly alongside the Profit and Loss Statement. It helps you track cash position, debt levels, and whether the business is growing in value over time.


---

## Next Steps


  * [Trial Balance](/docs/accounting/trial-balance) - Verify that all your ledger debits and credits are in balance.
  * [Profit and Loss Statement](/docs/accounting/profitandloss-statements.md) - See your revenue, expenses, and net profit for the period.
  * [General Ledger](/docs/accounting/ledger) - Drill down into any account to see its full transaction history.
  * [Ledgers](/docs/accounting/ledger.md) - Browse and manage your complete Chart of Accounts.
