docs/accounting/bank-accounts.description: Manage pharmacy bank accounts in MediFlux. Track balances, add accounts, and perform bank reconciliation to ensure accurate financial records.
docs/accounting/bank-accounts.body:
# Bank Accounts

The **Bank Accounts** page lets you add, manage, and view all **pharmacy bank accounts** linked to your business in **MediFlux**. Every account you add here automatically creates a ledger under **Cash & Bank → Bank Accounts** in your Chart of Accounts, so every deposit, withdrawal, and transfer is tracked in your books.

From this page, you can view current balances, filter by account type, set a default account for transactions, and reconcile your records against actual bank statements.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Accounting → Bank Accounts**.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Bank Accounts Overview](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/8a6fcbbe-df53-49d8-92c2-ea0ff4496478-Bank-accounts.png)
*Caption: Manage all connected pharmacy bank accounts, view current balances, and access reconciliation tools in MediFlux.*

---

## Search and Filter

Use the controls at the top to find accounts quickly.

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Search accounts...** | Search for a specific bank account by name or account number |
| **All account types** | Filter the list by account type: **Savings**, **Current**, **Fixed Deposit**, or **Recurring Deposit** |

![MediFlux Bank Account Type Filter](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/73d41b3c-0d05-4c45-88b1-27b9fdddf77b-search-filter-ba.png)
*Caption: Filter pharmacy bank accounts by type: Savings, Current, Fixed Deposit, or Recurring Deposit in MediFlux.*

---

## Summary Cards

Two cards sit above the table, giving you a quick view of your cash position:

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **In Current** | The total balance across all **Current** accounts |
| **Total Balance** | The combined balance across **all** bank accounts regardless of type |

> **[Note]** Fixed Deposits and Recurring Deposits are not included in the **In Current** total because they are not immediately liquid. They are included in **Total Balance**.

---

## Accounts Table

| Column | What it means |
|--------|---------------|
| **Account Name** | The name you gave the account, plus the bank name and branch below it |
| **Account Type** | Tag showing **Savings**, **Current**, **Fixed Deposit**, or **Recurring Deposit** |
| **Account Number** | The bank account number |
| **Balance** | The current ledger balance in MediFlux for this account |

Click the **three-dot menu** at the far right of any row to access account actions.

![MediFlux Bank Account Row Actions](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/c042f2d9-354a-47eb-b57f-f161cd548799-row-actions-ba.png)
*Caption: View details or set a specific pharmacy bank account as the default for transactions in MediFlux.*

| Action | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **View Details** | Opens the detailed ledger for this bank account, showing every transaction |
| **Set as Default** | Makes this the default bank account for new transactions. Only one account can be default at a time |

---

## Top Action Buttons

Four buttons sit in the top-right corner of the page:

| Button | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **View Rules** | Opens the list of existing reconciliation rules |
| **Add Rules** | Opens the dialog to create a new reconciliation rule |
| **Reconcile** | Opens the Bank Reconciliation screen |
| **Add Bank** | Opens the dialog to add a new bank account |

![MediFlux Bank Account Action Buttons](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/d54ceb0d-bcb0-4790-965b-777b2b776211-action-buttons.png)
*Caption: View reconciliation rules, add rules, reconcile transactions, or add a new pharmacy bank account in MediFlux.*

---

## Add a Bank Account

1. **Click Add Bank**

   Click **Add Bank** in the top-right corner.

2. **Fill in the details**

   - **Account Name**: A friendly name (e.g., Main Business Account)
       - **Account Number**: The full bank account number
       - **Bank Name**: The name of the bank
       - **IFSC Code**: The Indian Financial System Code for the branch
       - **Branch**: The branch name
       - **Account Type**: Select **Savings**, **Current**, **Fixed Deposit**, or **Recurring Deposit**

3. **Set as default (optional)**

   Check **Set as default bank account** if this should be the default for new transactions.

4. **Save**

   Click **Add Bank Account**.

![MediFlux Add Pharmacy Bank Account Dialog](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/a719cf14-d096-488b-8937-4cd6b9ca28e6-add-bank-acc.png)
*Caption: Fill in bank details to create a new pharmacy bank account and corresponding ledger in MediFlux.*

> **[Note]** When you add a bank account, MediFlux automatically creates a corresponding ledger under **Cash & Bank → Bank Accounts**. You do not need to create the ledger manually.

---

## Reconcile Your Bank Account

**Bank reconciliation** is the process of comparing the transactions recorded in MediFlux against the transactions shown on your actual bank statement. The goal is to identify and resolve differences between the two records.

Differences can happen for several reasons:

| Reason | Explanation |
|--------|-------------|
| **Pending transactions** | A cheque you deposited has not cleared yet, or a payment you made is still processing |
| **Bank fees or interest** | The bank charged a fee or credited interest that you have not yet recorded in MediFlux |
| **Errors in recording** | A transaction was entered with the wrong amount, wrong date, or posted to the wrong account |
| **Missing transactions** | A transaction happened at the bank but was never recorded in MediFlux |

### Open the Reconciliation Screen

Click **Reconcile** on the Bank Accounts page.

The updated **Bank Reconciliation** workspace opens, displaying account selection, reconciliation period, balance summaries, system ledger transactions, and bank statement controls.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Bank Reconciliation Workspace](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/d469bc03-3f7d-4f42-bfe8-2a261f795748-bank-reconciliation.png)
*Caption: Select a pharmacy bank account and period, review ledger and bank balances, and compare system transactions with an uploaded bank statement in MediFlux.*

### Select the Account and Period

At the top of the reconciliation workspace, you will find the following controls:

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Bank Account** | Select the bank account you want to reconcile |
| **Reconciliation Period** | Select the period for which you want to review transactions |
| **Workspace View** | Switch between **Split**, **Ledger**, and **Statement** views |

The reconciliation period is shown as **All Time** in the example screenshot.

### Workspace Views

You can change how transactions are displayed using the **Workspace View** control.

| View | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Split** | Displays the System Ledger and Bank Statement panels side by side |
| **Ledger** | Displays the system ledger workspace |
| **Statement** | Displays the bank statement workspace |

> **[Note]** The **Split** view is useful when comparing MediFlux transactions with the corresponding entries in your bank statement.

### Reconciliation Summary

Below the account selection controls, four summary cards display the current reconciliation information.

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **COA Ledger Balance** | The balance recorded in MediFlux's Chart of Accounts ledger for the selected bank account |
| **Actual Bank Balance** | An input field where you enter the balance from your official bank statement |
| **Difference** | The difference between the ledger balance and the actual bank balance |
| **Transaction Summary** | The number of loaded transactions in the Ledger and Statement |

#### Enter the Actual Bank Balance

In the **Actual Bank Balance** card, enter the balance shown on your official bank statement.

The **Difference** card helps you identify whether the balance recorded in MediFlux differs from the balance reported by your bank.

For example:

| Balance | Amount |
|---------|-------:|
| COA Ledger Balance | `₹25,000` |
| Actual Bank Balance | `₹24,500` |
| Difference | `₹500` |

In this example, you need to investigate the `₹500` difference before completing reconciliation.

> **[Note]** The amounts above are examples. Your actual balances depend on the selected bank account and its transactions.

### System Ledger

The **System Ledger** panel displays transactions recorded in MediFlux for the selected bank account.

At the top of this panel, you can search for transactions using the **Search ref, narration, ₹...** field.

You can also switch between three transaction tabs:

| Tab | What it shows |
|-----|---------------|
| **All** | All available system ledger transactions |
| **Reconciled** | Transactions that have already been reconciled |
| **Pending** | Transactions that are still pending reconciliation |

The number of transactions is displayed beside each tab.

#### System Ledger Table

| Column | What it means |
|--------|---------------|
| **Status** | Reconciliation status of the transaction |
| **Date** | Transaction date |
| **Ref / Vch** | Reference or voucher number |
| **Narration / Description** | Description of the transaction |
| **Debit** | Debit amount |
| **Credit** | Credit amount |
| **Balance** | Ledger balance shown for the transaction |
| **Action** | Available transaction actions |

The table may also display an **Opening Balance** row.

### Upload Your Bank Statement

The **Bank Statement** panel is used to load transactions from your official bank statement.

If no statement has been uploaded, the panel displays **No Statement Loaded** with an **Upload Statement CSV** button.

You can also access **Upload Statement CSV** from the top-right corner of the reconciliation page.

1. **Select the bank account**

   Choose the correct account from the **Bank Account** dropdown.

2. **Select the reconciliation period**

   Choose the period that matches the transactions you want to reconcile.

3. **Download your bank statement**

   Download the official statement for the selected account from your bank's website or mobile application in **CSV** format.

4. **Upload the statement**

   Click **Upload Statement CSV** and select the downloaded file.

5. **Review the statement transactions**

   Follow the on-screen instructions to load the statement.

       Once loaded, review its entries in the **Statement** workspace or switch to **Split** view to compare them with the System Ledger.

> **[Note]** The updated reconciliation interface provides an **Upload Statement CSV** option. Use a CSV file for this workflow.

### How Matching Works

Reconciliation involves comparing the transactions recorded in MediFlux with the transactions imported from your bank statement.

| Scenario | What it means | What to do |
|----------|---------------|------------|
| **Appears in both records** | The transaction is recorded in MediFlux and the bank statement | Verify the date, amount, and description before reconciling |
| **Only on bank statement** | The transaction is not found in the expected MediFlux ledger entries | Check for an existing entry under another reference before recording a missing transaction |
| **Only in MediFlux** | The transaction has not appeared in the bank statement | Check whether it is pending, uncleared, or incorrectly recorded |
| **Amounts do not match** | The records show different amounts for a transaction | Investigate bank fees, partial payments, or data entry errors |

> **[Warning: Check before recording a missing transaction]** A transaction may already exist in MediFlux under a different reference or narration. Search the existing ledger before creating another entry.

### Set Up Reconciliation Rules

Reconciliation rules help identify and match recurring transactions so you do not have to review the same types of entries manually every month.

1. **Click Add Rules**

   Click **Add Rules** on the Bank Accounts page.

2. **Fill in the rule**

   - **Bank Account**: The account this rule applies to
       - **Narration**: A keyword or phrase from the bank statement (e.g., "Bank charges")
       - **Entry Type**: **Debit** or **Credit**
       - **Amount Type**: **Exact**, **Contains**, or **Any**
       - **Amount**: Optional. Enter the exact amount if you chose **Exact**

3. **Save**

   Click **Add Rule**.

![MediFlux Bank Reconciliation Rule Setup](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/fa401419-3ec6-41ac-b332-3fc93dbef187-reconcilation-rule.png)
*Caption: Configure matching rules for recurring pharmacy bank transactions such as bank fees or EMIs in MediFlux.*

> **[Note]** Example: If your bank charges a fixed monthly fee of `₹500`, create a rule with Narration = "Bank charges", Entry Type = Debit, Amount Type = Exact, and Amount = `500`. MediFlux can use the rule to identify matching recurring transactions.

### Complete the Reconciliation

Once you have reviewed the statement transactions and investigated any differences, use the **Complete Reconciliation** button at the top-right corner of the workspace.

1. **Review the selected account**

   Confirm that the correct **Bank Account** and **Reconciliation Period** are selected.

2. **Check the balances**

   Compare the **COA Ledger Balance** with the **Actual Bank Balance** and review any difference.

3. **Review transaction statuses**

   Use the **Reconciled** and **Pending** tabs to check the transaction statuses.

4. **Click Complete Reconciliation**

   Click **Complete Reconciliation** and follow the on-screen confirmation instructions.

> **[Note]** Reconcile your bank accounts at least once a month, ideally when you receive your monthly bank statement.

---

## Common Mistakes

> **[Warning: Creating duplicate entries during reconciliation]** When you see a transaction on your bank statement that is missing from MediFlux, do not create a new journal entry without checking if it already exists under a different description. Search the system ledger first.

> **[Warning: Ignoring small differences]** A difference of even a few rupees may result from bank fees, interest, or rounding errors. Investigate these differences rather than leaving them unresolved.

> **[Warning: Uploading a statement for the wrong account]** Make sure the selected bank account matches the official statement you are uploading. Using a statement from another account can produce incorrect reconciliation results.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions


  ### What happens if I delete a bank account?

Deleting a bank account removes it from the Bank Accounts list but does not delete the corresponding ledger in your Chart of Accounts. Historical transactions remain intact and can still be viewed in the General Ledger.
  ### Can I reconcile multiple bank accounts at once?

No. Reconciliation is done one account at a time. Select the account from the **Bank Account** dropdown and upload the statement for that specific account.
  ### What file format does the statement import support?

The updated Bank Reconciliation interface provides **Upload Statement CSV**. Download your bank statement in CSV format to use this option.
  ### Why is my MediFlux balance different from my bank balance?

Common causes include pending cheques, unrecorded bank fees, missing transactions, or entries recorded with the wrong amount or date. Use Bank Reconciliation to identify and investigate these differences.
  ### What is the difference between COA Ledger Balance and Actual Bank Balance?

**COA Ledger Balance** is the balance recorded in MediFlux's Chart of Accounts.

    **Actual Bank Balance** is the balance shown on your official bank statement, which you enter in the reconciliation workspace.
  ### What is the difference between Split, Ledger, and Statement views?

**Split** displays the System Ledger and Bank Statement side by side.

    **Ledger** focuses on the transactions recorded in MediFlux.

    **Statement** focuses on the imported bank statement transactions.
  ### What is the difference between a Current account and a Savings account?

In MediFlux, the type is for your own organization and reporting. **Current** accounts are typically business accounts used for daily operations. **Savings** accounts are lower-transaction accounts. **Fixed Deposit** and **Recurring Deposit** are savings instruments with different deposit arrangements.


---

## Next Steps


  * [General Ledger](/docs/accounting/ledger) - View the complete transaction history for any bank account ledger.
  * [Ledgers](/docs/accounting/ledger.md) - Browse the Chart of Accounts and see how bank accounts fit into the structure.
  * [Add a Journal Entry](/docs/accounting/add-journal-entry) - Manually record bank fees, transfers, and other transactions.
  * [Trial Balance](/docs/accounting/trial-balance) - Verify that your bank account balances are reflected correctly in the overall books.

docs/accounting/dashboard.title: Accounting Dashboard
docs/accounting/dashboard.description: View your pharmacy accounting dashboard in MediFlux. Track total revenue, expenses, net profit, cash flow, and financial alerts easily.
docs/accounting/dashboard.body:
# Accounting Dashboard

The **Accounting Dashboard** gives you a live snapshot of your **pharmacy's financial health** in **MediFlux**. At a glance, you can see total revenue, expenses, net profit, and cash flow, plus trend charts and any active financial alerts.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Accounting → Dashboard**.

> **[Note]** A newly initialized store will show `₹0.00` across all cards and empty charts until you start recording sales, purchases, and other transactions.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Accounting Dashboard Overview](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/7207c33c-9d1a-4f28-b2c5-a01b81e59ddc-accounting-dashboard.png)
*Caption: Summary cards, revenue vs expense trend, monthly comparison, expense distribution, and financial alerts for a pharmacy in MediFlux.*

---

## Summary Cards

Four cards at the top show the key numbers for the selected period.

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Total Revenue** | All income earned (sales and other income) |
| **Expenses** | All costs incurred in the same period |
| **Net Profit** | Total Revenue minus Expenses |
| **Cash Flow** | Net movement of cash and bank balances |

Each card also shows a small trend indicator (or **N/A** when there is not enough data yet).

---

## Revenue vs. Expense Trend

This area chart shows how revenue and expenses have moved over time.

- **Green** area = Revenue
- **Orange / red** area = Expenses

Use the time filter in the top-right of the chart (**All Time** or other available ranges) to change the period.

The chart helps you spot periods where expenses rose faster than revenue or where revenue spiked.

![MediFlux Revenue vs. Expense Trend Chart](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/6f9f1c37-d647-4755-82a3-9f4fd047a039-expense-vs-revenue.png)
*Caption: Area chart comparing pharmacy revenue and expenses over the selected period in the MediFlux Accounting Dashboard.*

---

## Monthly Comparison

The bar chart compares total revenue and total expenses for each month.

- Green bar = Revenue
- Red bar = Expenses

This view is useful for identifying cost spikes or months where profit was unusually high or low.

The same time filter (**All Time**, etc.) applies to this chart.

---

## Expense Distribution

The pie chart breaks your total expenses into categories for the selected period.

Each slice shows the amount spent in that category. Hover over a slice to see the exact value and percentage.

This helps you quickly see which expense categories are consuming the largest share of your costs.

---

## Financial Alerts

At the bottom of the dashboard, MediFlux surfaces important warnings when something needs attention.

| Situation | What you see |
|-----------|--------------|
| Everything is healthy | “No financial alerts at the moment. Everything looks good!” |
| Cash or bank balance is zero or negative | **Low Liquidity**: Cash and bank balance is at or below zero. |

![MediFlux Pharmacy Financial Alerts Dashboard](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/d72e8724-87b2-4ab4-b6d8-11baa93bf8b5-financial-alerts.png)
*Caption: Zero values in all cards, empty charts, and a Low Liquidity alert on a newly initialized MediFlux pharmacy store.*

---

## Common Mistakes

> **[Warning: Expecting data on a brand-new store]** Until you record sales, purchases, payments, or journal entries, every card will show `₹0.00` and the charts will be empty. This is normal.

> **[Warning: Ignoring the Low Liquidity alert]** If the dashboard shows **Low Liquidity**, your cash and bank balances are at or below zero. Check the Daybook and Cash & Bank accounts before making further payments.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions


  ### What period do the summary cards use?

The cards and charts follow the time filter selected on each chart (for example, **All Time**). Change the filter to focus on a specific range.
  ### Why does Net Profit look different from the Profit & Loss statement?

The dashboard gives a high-level snapshot. For a full breakdown by account, open the **Profit & Loss** report, which includes every income and expense ledger for the exact period you choose.
  ### Can I click the charts to drill down?

The charts are visual summaries. To see the underlying transactions, go to the **Daybook**, **Journal Entries**, or the individual ledger of any account.
  ### What should I do when I see a Low Liquidity alert?

Review your Cash on Hand, Bank Accounts, and Digital Wallets in the Chart of Accounts or Daybook. Record any missing receipts or transfer funds if needed.


---

## Next Steps


  * [Profit & Loss](/docs/accounting/profitandloss-statements.md) - See the full income and expense breakdown that feeds the dashboard numbers.
  * [Daybook](/docs/accounting/daybook) - View every transaction that contributed to revenue, expenses, and cash flow.
  * Journal Entries - Inspect the individual journals behind the dashboard figures.
  * [Balance Sheet](/docs/accounting/balance-sheet) - Check your assets, liabilities, and equity position.

docs/accounting/daybook.title: Daybook
docs/accounting/daybook.description: Track daily pharmacy financial transactions in MediFlux. View the Daybook for money received, spent, customer dues, and journal entries easily.
docs/accounting/daybook.body:
# Daybook

The **Daybook** is a chronological list of every **pharmacy financial transaction** that affected your accounts during the selected period in **MediFlux**. It shows money that came in, money that went out, new customer dues, and new supplier dues, along with the full debit and credit details of each entry.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Accounting → Daybook**.

> **[Note]** By default, the Daybook shows the **current month**. A newly initialized store will usually show only the Accounting Initialization entry and zero values in most summary cards.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Accounting Daybook Overview](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/0b81ef48-9199-4738-bb2d-bed8aa2e8b65-daybook.png)
*Caption: Daybook overview showing daily financial transactions, money received, and dues for a pharmacy in MediFlux.*

---

## Summary Cards

Four cards at the top give you a quick overview of the selected period.

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Money Received** | Total cash and bank inflow during the period |
| **Money Spent** | Total cash and bank outflow during the period |
| **Customer Dues Added** | Total new amounts customers owe you (Amount to Receive) |
| **Supplier Dues Added** | Total new amounts you owe suppliers (Amount to Pay) |

![MediFlux Daybook Summary Cards](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/5db9e538-bf6c-4a1b-8f7d-b84a58ea1ddd-daybook-summarycards.png)
*Caption: Summary cards for money received, money spent, customer dues, and supplier dues in the MediFlux pharmacy Daybook.*

---

## Filtering the Daybook

Use the controls at the top to change the period or narrow the list.

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Date range** | Select the period. Defaults to the current month. Click to open the calendar with quick presets |
| **Search description, account or...** | Find entries by description text, account name, or journal ID |
| **All entry types** | Filter by how the entry was created |

### Date Range Picker

Click the date range to open the calendar. You can pick custom dates or use the quick options:

**Today · Yesterday · Last 7 days · Last 14 days · Last 30 days · This Week · Last Week · This Month · Last Month**

Click **Apply** to update the Daybook.

![MediFlux Daybook Date Range Picker](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/06d71b6e-46f8-4cee-8757-51ab4b25d37e-date-range-filter.png)
*Caption: Calendar with quick filter options for common periods in the MediFlux pharmacy Daybook.*

### Entry Type Filter

| Type | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Manual entry** | Created by a user through Add Journal |
| **Sale** | Automatically generated from a sale |
| **Purchase** | Automatically generated from a purchase |
| **Payment** | Payment made to a supplier or other party |
| **Receipt** | Money received from a customer or other party |
| **Opening balance** | Entries created during account setup |
| **Adjustment** | Stock adjustments, credit notes, and similar corrections |

---

## Understanding the Table

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Date** | Date and time of the entry |
| **Entry** | Journal ID plus a type badge (MANUAL, AUTO SALE, AUTO PURCHASE, etc.) |
| **Description** | Short explanation of the transaction. Some descriptions include a clickable **Sale** or **Purchase** link that opens the related document |
| **Debit** | Account(s) debited. A small `+N` badge shows how many accounts are involved when there are more than one |
| **Credit** | Account(s) credited. A small `+N` badge shows how many accounts are involved when there are more than one |
| **Amount** | Value of the entry |

### Clickable Sale and Purchase Links

When a description contains a **Sale** or **Purchase** link (shown with an arrow icon), click it to open that specific sale or purchase document. This lets you jump straight from the Daybook to the original transaction.

---

## Example Entries of a Test Store

| Date | Entry | Description | Debit | Credit | Amount |
|------|-------|-------------|-------|--------|--------|
| 31 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00219` MANUAL | Return Purchase | Mediflux | Purchase Return | ₹900.00 |
| 31 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00218` MANUAL | Returned Purchase | Digital Wallets | Purchase Return | ₹6,500.00 |
| 31 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00217` MANUAL | Advance Amount To Supplier | Supplier Advances | Mediflux | ₹1,500.00 |
| 31 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00216` MANUAL | Purchase Drugs | Mediflux | Purchase Cost of Medicines | ₹500.00 |
| 25 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00197` AUTO SALE | Sale 2026/202 To Mujtaba | Purchase Cost of Medicines | Medicine Inventory | ₹20.00 |
| 25 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00190` AUTO CREDIT NOTE | Credit Note CN/2026/020 To Aleeza | Trade Creditors | Round Off Gain | ₹9.50 |
| 25 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00182` STOCK ADJUSTMENT | Bulk Stock Adjustment | Medicine Inventory | Stock Adjustment Gain | ₹40,507.96 |
| 24 Aug 2026 | `JE-2026-08-00181` AUTO RETURN SALE | Journal Entry On Returning Sale 2026/200 | Medicine Inventory | Purchase Cost of Medicines | ₹361.31 |

![MediFlux Auto-Generated Daybook Entries](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/e5a9dcc3-e9d8-4fdf-a9bc-62113d70213a-daybook-entries.png)
*Caption: Auto-generated pharmacy sale, credit note, stock adjustment, and return sale entries with linked descriptions in MediFlux.*

---

## Newly Initialized Stores

On a store that has just completed accounting setup, you will typically see:

- Summary cards mostly at `₹0.00` (except Supplier Dues Added if opening balances were entered)
- A single entry with type **ACCOUNTING INITIALIZATION**
- Description: Entries Added On Initialization Of Chart Of Accounts

This is expected. More rows appear as soon as you record sales, purchases, payments, and manual journals.

![MediFlux Newly Initialized Store Daybook](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/f0f11374-3804-4cc7-b374-54a262effe94-new-accounting.png)
*Caption: Single Accounting Initialization entry with zero values in most summary cards for a new MediFlux pharmacy store.*

---

## Common Mistakes

> **[Warning: Looking at the wrong date range]** The Daybook defaults to the **current month**. If the list looks empty or incomplete, open the date range picker and select a wider period or **Last Month**.

> **[Warning: Missing the linked sale or purchase]** Some descriptions show a **Sale** or **Purchase** link with an arrow. Clicking the link opens the original document. If you only read the text and ignore the link, you miss the fastest way to see full transaction details.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions


  ### What is the difference between Daybook and Journal Entries?

The **Journal Entries** page focuses on the list of journals with status and who posted them. The **Daybook** adds the money-flow summary cards (received, spent, dues) and shows the debit and credit accounts side by side for every entry, making it easier to see the daily impact on cash, bank, customers, and suppliers.
  ### Why do some debit or credit cells show +1, +2, +3?

The `+N` badge means the entry touches more than one account on that side. Hover or click to see the full list of accounts involved.
  ### Can I export the Daybook?

Use the date range and entry-type filters to show exactly the rows you need, then export from the related Journal Entries page or use your browser print function if a direct export button is not available on Daybook.
  ### Why is Money Received or Money Spent showing zero?

These cards only count actual cash and bank movements. Credit sales, stock adjustments, and pure accrual entries do not increase Money Received or Money Spent.


---

## Next Steps


  * Journal Entries - View every journal with status, type, and who posted it.
  * [Add Journal Entry](/docs/accounting/add-journal-entry) - Create a manual debit and credit entry.
  * [General Ledger](/docs/accounting/ledger) - See the full history and running balance of any single account.
  * [Profit & Loss](/docs/accounting/profitandloss-statements.md) - See how the transactions in the Daybook flow into your income and expenses.

docs/accounting/general-ledger.title: General Ledger
docs/accounting/general-ledger.description: View your pharmacy general ledger in MediFlux. Track detailed transaction history, running balances, and audit individual ledger accounts easily.
docs/accounting/general-ledger.body:
# General Ledger

## What Is the General Ledger

The **General Ledger** is the complete transaction history of a single **pharmacy ledger account** in **MediFlux**. Every debit and credit that hits that account is recorded here in chronological order, with a running balance that updates after each entry. Use it to verify how an account's balance was built, trace transactions back to their source, and reconcile figures against your bank statements or supplier records.

---

## Open the General Ledger

Go to **Accounting → General Ledger** from the left sidebar.

On your first visit, a **Select Ledger** dialog opens automatically because no account is pre-selected.

![MediFlux Pharmacy General Ledger Account Selection](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/c7c9b0e5-2c2d-4d77-80ff-00d0d62db372-general-ledger.png)
*Caption: Select Ledger dialog showing only leaf-level accounts that can be chosen for the MediFlux pharmacy general ledger.*

The dialog lists every leaf-level account. Each entry shows the breadcrumb path, such as `Accounts Receivable > Customer Receivables` or `Cash & Bank > Bank Accounts > Test Bank`, along with the account type and normal balance tags. Click any account to load its ledger.

> **Note:** You cannot select parent groups like **Cash & Bank** or **Inventory** directly. You must select the specific child account, such as **Cash on Hand** or **Medicine Inventory**.

---

## Switch to a Different Account

Click **Change** in the account header to reopen the **Select Ledger** dialog and pick a different account at any time.

---

## Filter and Search Transactions

Use the filter bar at the top of the page to narrow down what you see.

![MediFlux Pharmacy General Ledger Filter Bar](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/92e19662-80fc-439e-88fd-c969f7588620-GL-FILTERPANEL.png)
*Caption: Search, date range, Posted/Reversals toggle, Filters, and Export controls for the MediFlux general ledger.*

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Search** | Search by transaction description or journal entry number |
| **Date range** | Pick a custom period. Defaults to the current month |
| **Posted / Reversals** | Toggle between **Posted** (regular entries) and **Reversals** (reversed or correcting entries) |
| **Filters** | Opens advanced filter options for narrowing the transaction list |
| **Export** | Download the ledger data as **PDF Document** or **Excel Sheet** |

### Search

Type a description or journal number (for example `JE-2026-08-00196`) in the search box to instantly filter the table.

![MediFlux General Ledger Search Bar](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/48310dcd-632a-44dc-9771-324902eb22e3-GK-SEARCHBAR.png)
*Caption: Search the pharmacy general ledger by transaction description or journal entry number in MediFlux.*

### Date Range

Click the date range control to open the calendar. You can select custom dates or use quick presets such as **Today**, **This Month**, **Last Month**, etc.

![MediFlux General Ledger Date Range Picker](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/f857e8f5-955a-4556-a321-00aa5940aa8b-GL-DATERANGE.png)
*Caption: Choose a custom period or use the quick filter options for the pharmacy general ledger in MediFlux.*

### Posted / Reversals Toggle

Use this control to switch between regular posted entries and reversal entries.

![MediFlux General Ledger Posted and Reversals Toggle](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/6566a9ac-9092-41e3-90a8-fc2052653b94-gl-toggle.png)
*Caption: Toggle between regular posted entries and reversal entries in the MediFlux pharmacy general ledger.*

### Export

Click **Export** and choose **PDF Document** or **Excel Sheet**.

![MediFlux General Ledger Export Options](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/221cd730-0e53-46e9-aea9-242d61451b9f-GL-EXPORT.png)
*Caption: Download the pharmacy general ledger transaction history as a PDF or Excel file from MediFlux.*

---

## Read the Account Header and Summary

Below the filter bar, the header shows the selected account name, its type tag (such as `CURRENT ASSET` or `EXPENSE`), and its normal balance tag (`DEBIT NORMAL` or `CREDIT NORMAL`).

![MediFlux Pharmacy General Ledger Account Header](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/def6f878-bcd8-4489-b673-a8dd559320c7-acctype-gl.png)
*Caption: General Ledger header for Customer Receivables showing transaction history, account type, and normal balance in MediFlux.*

Four summary cards sit below the header:

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Opening Balance** | The balance at the start of the selected date range |
| **Total Debits** | Sum of all debit entries in the selected period |
| **Total Credits** | Sum of all credit entries in the selected period |
| **Closing Balance** | The balance after all entries in the selected period |

![MediFlux General Ledger Summary Cards](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/1c676c0c-4881-407f-9d3b-82257d812728-gl-summarycards.png)
*Caption: Summary cards showing Opening Balance, Total Debits, Total Credits, and Closing Balance for the selected period in MediFlux.*

---

## Read the Transaction Table

The table lists every journal entry posted to this account, sorted by date with the most recent at the top.

| Column | What it means |
|--------|---------------|
| **Date** | The date the journal entry was posted |
| **Journal** | The unique journal entry identifier, such as `JE-2026-08-00196` |
| **Description** | A brief explanation of what the entry represents |
| **Type** | The journal entry type, such as `AUTO SALE`, `AUTO CREDIT NOTE`, `STOCK DELETION`, or `ACCOUNTING INITIALIZATION` |
| **Source** | The module or document that triggered the entry, such as **Sale**, **Credit Note**, **Appointment**, or **None** |
| **Debit** | Amount debited to this account. Shown in green for debit-normal accounts, red for credit-normal accounts |
| **Credit** | Amount credited to this account. Shown in red for debit-normal accounts, green for credit-normal accounts |
| **Balance** | The running balance after this entry. Always shows `Dr` or `Cr` to indicate which side the balance sits on |

> **How to read the running balance:** The balance column updates after every row. If you are viewing a debit-normal account, debits add to the balance and credits subtract from it. For a credit-normal account, credits add and debits subtract.

Click the **Journal** number in any row to open the full journal entry. This shows all the accounts that were debited and credited in that single transaction, not just the entries for the current ledger.

---

## How to Read Debit and Credit Entries

The direction of each entry depends on the account's **normal balance**.

### Debit-Normal Accounts

**Assets** and **Expenses** are debit-normal. Their balance increases when debited and decreases when credited.

| Account type | Normal balance | Debit means | Credit means |
|--------------|----------------|-------------|--------------|
| Asset | `Dr` | Balance increases | Balance decreases |
| Expense | `Dr` | Balance increases | Balance decreases |

#### Example: Customer Receivables

| Date | Journal | Description | Type | Source | Debit | Credit | Balance |
|------|---------|-------------|------|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| 31 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00220 | No Description | `MANUAL` | None | `₹200.00` | — | `₹94,781.31 Dr` |
| 31 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00210 | Appointment | `MANUAL` | None | `₹500.00` | `₹500.00` | `₹94,581.31 Dr` |
| 26 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00196 | AR Created For Appointment 6a8d6... | `AUTO APPOINTMENT` | Appointment | — | — | `₹94,581.31 Dr` |
| 25 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00191 | Customer Receivable Updated By D... | `AUTO CUSTOMER` | Customer | — | `₹11,216.86` | `₹94,581.31 Dr` |

> **Opening Balance** is the balance at the start of the selected date range (shown at the bottom of the list).  
> **Closing Balance** is the balance after all entries in the selected period (shown at the top of the list).

In this example the closing balance is `₹94,781.31 Dr`. Because this is a debit-normal asset account, a positive debit balance means customers still owe the pharmacy this amount.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Customer Receivables Ledger](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/1b1f1b33-fccd-4a69-b806-f6b6ee30088b-GL-ENTRIES.png)
*Caption: Customer Receivables ledger showing how debits increase what customers owe and credits decrease it in MediFlux.*

#### Example: Stock Loss & Adjustments

| Date | Journal | Description | Type | Source | Debit | Credit | Balance |
|------|---------|-------------|------|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| 24 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00174 | Inventory Loss Due To Bulk Drug Del... | `STOCK DELETION` | None | `₹3,386.25` | — | `₹8,962.83 Dr` |
| 19 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00139 | Stock Adjustment Loss Was Update... | `AUTO SALE` | Sale | `₹5,576.58` | — | `₹5,576.58 Dr` |

![MediFlux Pharmacy Stock Loss and Adjustments Ledger](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/095b3fe3-633b-42d2-a80b-e91b35d51c03-SL-ADJUSMENTS.GL.png)
*Caption: Stock Loss & Adjustments ledger showing only debit entries for a debit-normal expense account in MediFlux.*

> **Closing balance:** `₹8,962.83 Dr`. Expenses always carry a debit balance.

---

### Credit-Normal Accounts

**Liabilities**, **Equity**, and **Revenue** are credit-normal. Their balance increases when credited and decreases when debited.

| Account type | Normal balance | Debit means | Credit means |
|--------------|----------------|-------------|--------------|
| Liability | `Cr` | Balance decreases | Balance increases |
| Equity | `Cr` | Balance decreases | Balance increases |
| Revenue | `Cr` | Balance decreases | Balance increases |

#### Example: Purchase Return

| Date | Journal | Description | Type | Source | Debit | Credit | Balance |
|------|---------|-------------|------|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| 25 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00190 | Purchase Return Via Credit Note | `AUTO CREDIT NOTE` | Credit Note | — | `₹190.00` | `₹3,902.99 Cr` |
| 21 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00145 | Purchase Return Via Credit Note | `AUTO CREDIT NOTE` | Credit Note | — | `₹2,890.00` | `₹3,712.99 Cr` |
| 19 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00134 | Purchase Return Via Credit Note | `AUTO CREDIT NOTE` | Credit Note | — | `₹515.94` | `₹822.99 Cr` |
| 19 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00133 | Purchase Return Via Credit Note | `AUTO CREDIT NOTE` | Credit Note | — | `₹307.05` | `₹307.05 Cr` |

![MediFlux Pharmacy Purchase Return Ledger](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/1599cc72-3552-4f1f-bc3a-728ed2373802-purchase-return-GL.png)
*Caption: Purchase Return ledger showing only credit entries for a credit-normal contra-asset account in MediFlux.*

> **Opening balance:** `₹0.00 Dr`  
> **Closing balance:** `₹11,302.99 Cr`

Purchase Return is a **contra-asset** account (Credit Normal). Credits increase its balance and reduce the total value of inventory on your books.

#### Example: GST Output CGST

| Date | Journal | Description | Type | Source | Debit | Credit | Balance |
|------|---------|-------------|------|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| 25 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00197 | CGST @2.5% (Slab 5%) | `AUTO SALE` | Sale | — | `₹0.48` | `₹12,431.81 Cr` |
| 25 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00184 | CGST @5% (Slab 10%) | `AUTO SALE` | Sale | — | `₹2.56` | `₹12,431.33 Cr` |
| 24 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00181 | CGST @6% (Slab 12%) | `AUTO RETURN SALE` | Sale | `₹10.20` | — | `₹12,428.77 Cr` |
| 24 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00180 | CGST @6% (Slab 12%) | `AUTO SALE` | Sale | — | `₹10.20` | `₹12,438.97 Cr` |
| 24 Aug 2026 | JE-2026-08-00180 | CGST @2.5% (Slab 5%) | `AUTO SALE` | Sale | — | `₹0.42` | `₹12,428.77 Cr` |

![MediFlux Pharmacy GST Output CGST Ledger](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/79e9df94-becf-4336-b60a-20308325962c-gst-gl.png)
*Caption: GST Output CGST ledger showing credits from sales and debits from returns for a credit-normal liability account in MediFlux.*

> **Opening balance** is the balance at the start of the selected date range (`₹0.00 Dr`).  
> **Closing balance** is the balance after all entries in the selected period (`₹12,435.38 Cr`).

This is a credit-normal liability account. A credit balance means the pharmacy has collected this much CGST from customers and must remit it to the government.

When a customer returns a product, the related tax is reversed with a **debit** entry (see the `AUTO RETURN SALE` row on 24 Aug). This reduces the liability.

---

## Newly Initialized Accounts

If you have just set up the Accounting module and have not yet recorded any sales, purchases, or journal entries, your ledgers will look sparse. A newly initialized account typically shows only one entry:

| Date | Journal | Description | Type | Source | Debit | Credit | Balance |
|------|---------|-------------|------|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| — | — | Accounts Receivable Created On Ini... | `ACCOUNTING INITIALIZATION` | None | — | — | `₹0.00 Dr` |

This is a system-generated entry that creates the ledger account in your books. It carries no monetary value. Once you start recording transactions, real debits and credits will populate the table and the balance will move away from zero.

> **Tip:** For a debit-normal account like **Medicine Inventory**, the first real transaction will typically be a debit from your opening stock balance or your first purchase. For a credit-normal account like **GST Payable**, the first real transaction will be a credit from your first taxable sale.

For some accounts, the table may show **No entries found** with the message *"Try adjusting the filters or date range."* This happens when the account has no activity in the selected date range, or when it was initialized but has not yet received any transactions. Widen the date range or check back after recording sales, purchases, or journal entries.

![MediFlux General Ledger No Entries Found State](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/ee7eda58-a99e-441c-83f0-479f1fbc123d-Noentriesfound-GL.png)
*Caption: General Ledger showing No entries found empty state. Widen your date range or record transactions to populate the MediFlux ledger.*

---

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

> **[Warning: Narrow date range hiding transactions]** If you cannot find a transaction you know exists, check your **Date range** filter. It defaults to the current month, so older entries are hidden. Click the date picker and widen the range to see everything.

> **[Warning: Misreading green and red colors]** Green does not always mean good and red does not always mean bad. For a debit-normal account like **Cash on Hand**, debits are green and credits are red. For a credit-normal account like **GST Payable**, credits are green and debits are red. Always check the `DEBIT NORMAL` or `CREDIT NORMAL` tag in the header before interpreting colors.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions


  ### Why does the Select Ledger dialog open automatically?

The General Ledger page needs to know which account you want to view. Since there is no default account, the dialog opens on your first visit so you can pick one. After selecting, the dialog closes and the ledger loads. You can change the account anytime by clicking **Change**.
  ### What is the difference between Debit Normal and Credit Normal?

**Debit Normal** means the account balance increases when debited and decreases when credited. Asset and expense accounts are debit normal. **Credit Normal** means the account balance increases when credited and decreases when debited. Liability, equity, and revenue accounts are credit normal.
  ### Why are some amounts shown in green and others in red?

The color indicates whether the entry is increasing or decreasing the account balance relative to its normal balance. For a debit-normal account, debits are green (increasing) and credits are red (decreasing). For a credit-normal account, credits are green (increasing) and debits are red (decreasing).
  ### Can I view the full journal entry behind a row?

Click on the **Journal** number in any row to open the full journal entry. This shows all the accounts that were debited and credited in that single transaction, not just the entries for the current ledger.
  ### What does the Balance column represent?

The Balance column shows the running balance of the account after each transaction, calculated from top to bottom (most recent first). It tells you what the account balance was at that point in time.


---

## Next Steps


  * [Ledgers](/docs/accounting/ledger.md) - Browse and manage your complete Chart of Accounts.
  * [Add a Journal Entry](/docs/accounting/add-journal-entry) - Manually record transactions that post to multiple ledgers.
  * [Trial Balance](/docs/accounting/trial-balance) - See all ledger balances in one place to verify your books.
  * [Daybook](/docs/accounting/daybook) - View all journal entries across all accounts in chronological order.

docs/accounting/itc-reversals.title: ITC Reversals
docs/accounting/itc-reversals.description: Manage pharmacy ITC reversals in MediFlux. Track and reverse input tax credit for expired stock, charity, and personal use to ensure GST compliance.
docs/accounting/itc-reversals.body:
# ITC Reversals

The **ITC Reversals** page lists every pending **Input Tax Credit (ITC) reversal** that MediFlux has detected for your **pharmacy**. You can mark items as not applicable or reverse the credit so your GST liability stays accurate and compliant.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Accounting → ITC Reversals**.

---

## What Is ITC Reversal?

When you buy medicines or goods, you pay GST to the supplier. That GST is your **Input Tax Credit (ITC)**. You can normally use it to reduce the GST you collect from customers.

Sometimes you are **not allowed** to keep that credit. In those cases, the law requires you to **reverse** the ITC. This means you add the credit back to your GST liability (you effectively pay it back to the government).

Common situations in a pharmacy where ITC must be reversed:

| Situation | Why reversal is required |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| **Expired Stock** | Medicines that expired and cannot be sold. ITC claimed on their purchase must be reversed. |
| **Charity / Free Samples** | Goods given free or donated. No taxable supply is made, so ITC is not allowed. |
| **Personal Use** | Stock used for personal or non-business purposes. |
| **Other Non-Business Use** | Any case where the goods are not used for making taxable supplies. |

MediFlux automatically detects these cases (especially from stock adjustments, expired stock write-offs, and certain debit notes) and adds them to this page as **Pending** lines so you can review and act on them.

---

## Summary Cards

Three cards at the top show the current state of the list.

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Pending Lines** | Number of ITC reversal lines still waiting for action |
| **Total GST Value** | Combined CGST + SGST + IGST of all pending lines |
| **Selected GST Value** | GST value of the rows you have currently checked |

---

## Understanding the Table

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Checkbox** | Select one or more rows for bulk actions |
| **Date** | Date the event that triggered the potential reversal occurred |
| **Type** | Reason for the reversal: Expired, Charity, Personal Use, etc. |
| **Value** | Taxable value of the goods involved |
| **CGST** | Central GST portion of the credit to be reversed |
| **SGST** | State GST portion of the credit to be reversed |
| **IGST** | Integrated GST portion (usually ₹0.00 for intra-state) |
| **Status** | Current state of the line (Pending) |
| **Actions** | **Mark N/A** or **Reverse** for that single line |

---

## What You Can Do

### Reverse a Single Line

Click **Reverse** on any row. MediFlux creates the necessary journal entry that reverses the ITC (debiting the appropriate GST expense/reversal account and crediting the Input GST accounts). The line is then removed from the pending list.

### Mark a Line as N/A

Click **Mark N/A** if the line should not be reversed (for example, the stock was later sold, or the detection was incorrect). The line is cleared from the pending list without creating a reversal entry.

### Bulk Actions

| Button | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Mark all N/A** | Marks every pending line as not applicable |
| **Reverse all** | Reverses ITC for every pending line in one go |

You can also check individual boxes and then use the bulk buttons if they support selected rows.

Each row has two row-level buttons — **Mark N/A** and **Reverse** — plus bulk **Mark all N/A** and **Reverse all** buttons above the table.

---

## Example Pending Lines

| Date | Type | Value | CGST | SGST | IGST | Status |
|------|------|-------|------|------|------|--------|
| 19 Aug 2026 | Expired | ₹5,576.58 | ₹538.02 | ₹538.02 | ₹0.00 | Pending |
| 19 Aug 2026 | Charity | ₹200.00 | ₹14.13 | ₹14.13 | ₹0.00 | Pending |
| 20 Aug 2026 | Personal Use | ₹773.80 | ₹53.57 | ₹53.57 | ₹0.00 | Pending |

In this example, the **Total GST Value** is ₹1,211.44 (sum of all CGST + SGST).

---

## How the Reversal Works in the Books

When you click **Reverse**:

1. MediFlux calculates the GST amounts (CGST, SGST, or IGST) that were originally claimed as ITC.
2. It posts a journal entry that:
   - Debits an ITC reversal / GST expense account
   - Credits the Input GST accounts (GST Input CGST, GST Input SGST, or GST Input IGST)
3. Your net ITC balance decreases and your GST liability increases by the same amount.
4. The line disappears from the ITC Reversals pending list.

This keeps your GSTR-3B and other GST returns accurate.

---

## Common Mistakes

> **[Warning: Leaving expired stock reversals pending]** Expired medicines are one of the most common reasons for ITC reversal in pharmacies. Leaving them in Pending status for a long time can cause your GST returns to understate liability.

> **[Warning: Reversing lines that should be Mark N/A]** Only reverse lines that genuinely require ITC reversal. If stock was later sold or the detection is wrong, use **Mark N/A** instead of **Reverse**.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions


  ### Does reversing ITC create a journal entry?

Yes. Every time you click **Reverse**, MediFlux posts a proper journal entry so the change is fully reflected in your ledgers, Trial Balance, and GST reports.
  ### What happens if I click Mark all N/A by mistake?

The pending lines are cleared without reversing credit. If you still need to reverse some of them, you will have to handle the reversal manually through a journal entry or wait for the system to re-detect the case.
  ### Why is IGST usually zero?

Most pharmacy purchases are intra-state, so only CGST and SGST apply. IGST appears when the original purchase was inter-state.
  ### Is this the same as a credit note from a supplier?

No. A supplier credit note reduces your purchase and the related ITC automatically. The ITC Reversals page handles cases where **you** must reverse ITC because of how the goods were later used or written off (expiry, charity, personal use, etc.).


---

## Next Steps


  * Journal Entries - View the reversal journals created when you reverse ITC.
  * [Daybook](/docs/accounting/daybook) - See the daily impact of ITC reversals on your accounts.
  * [Profit & Loss](/docs/accounting/profitandloss-statements.md) - ITC reversal expenses appear in your expense section.
  * [Chart of Accounts](/docs/accounting/ledger.md) - Locate the Input GST and ITC reversal accounts.

docs/accounting/journals.description: View and manage pharmacy journal entries in MediFlux. Search, filter, and export manual and auto-generated accounting ledgers easily.
docs/accounting/journals.body:
# Journals The **Journals** page is where you can see every **pharmacy journal entry** that has been posted to your ledgers in **MediFlux**. This includes manual journals you create yourself, automatic entries generated from purchases and sales, and the one-time initialization entry that is created when your Chart of Accounts is first set up. Navigate here from the sidebar: **Accounting → Journals**. > **[Note]** By default, the page shows entries for the **current month**. If your store is newly initialized, you will usually see only one entry: the Accounting Initialization journal. ![MediFlux Pharmacy Journal Entries List](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/76d5d379-b67d-4411-8b93-b126f340d805-journals.png) *Caption: Search, date range, status, and type filters for pharmacy journal entries in the MediFlux accounting module.* --- ## Adding a New Journal Entry Click **+ Add Journal** in the top-right corner to create a manual journal entry. This opens the journal entry form where you select debit and credit accounts, enter amounts, and add a description. Once posted, the entry appears in this list with status **POSTED** and type **MANUAL**. ![MediFlux Add Pharmacy Journal Entry Button](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/e3071f6e-450f-4071-b4db-d000e75b6206-add-journal.png) *Caption: Click + Add Journal in the top-right to create a manual accounting entry in MediFlux.* --- ## Searching and Filtering Use the controls at the top of the page to narrow down the list. | Control | What it does | |---------|--------------| | **Search entry or description...** | Find journals by Journal ID or by the text in the description | | **Date range** | Choose the period to view. Defaults to the current month. Click to open the calendar | | **All Statuses** | Filter by status: Posted, Draft, Reversed, or Cancelled | | **All Types** | Filter by account type categories such as Current Asset, Non Current Asset, Current Liability, Equity, Revenue, or Expense | | **Clear** | Remove all active filters and return to the default view | | **Export** | Download the current list as PDF or Excel | ### Date Range Picker Click the date range to open the calendar. You can: - Select custom start and end dates - Use quick presets: **Today**, **Yesterday**, **Last 7 days**, **Last 14 days**, **Last 30 days**, **This Week**, **Last Week**, **This Month**, **Last Month** Click **Apply** to update the list. ![MediFlux Journal Date Range Picker](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/48119dca-e2ab-4f51-9fa6-046dfbc5bd4d-date-range-picker.png) *Caption: Calendar with quick filter options for common periods in the MediFlux pharmacy Journals list.* ### Status Filter | Status | Meaning | |--------|---------| | **Posted** | The entry has been successfully posted to the ledgers | | **Draft** | The entry is saved but not yet posted | | **Reversed** | The original entry has been reversed | | **Cancelled** | The entry was cancelled and has no effect on the books | ![MediFlux Journal Status Filter](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/1cfb1b27-4677-4370-b077-042dd046a25b-all-statuses.png) *Caption: Filter pharmacy journal entries by Posted, Draft, Reversed, or Cancelled status in MediFlux.* ### Type Badges on Each Row Each journal shows a small badge under the Journal ID that tells you how it was created: | Badge | Meaning | |-------|---------| | **MANUAL** | Created by a user through **Add Journal** | | **AUTO PURCHASE** | Automatically generated when a purchase is recorded | | **AUTO PURCHASE REVERSAL** | Automatically created when a purchase is edited or reversed | | **ACCOUNTING INITIALIZATION** | Created once when the Chart of Accounts is first set up | --- ## Understanding the Table | Column | Description | |--------|-------------| | **JOURNAL ID** | Unique identifier (e.g. `JE-2026-08-00221`). The type badge appears below it | | **DATE** | Date and time the entry was posted | | **DESCRIPTION** | Short text explaining the entry. Some descriptions are clickable links that open the related purchase or document | | **STATUS** | Current status of the entry (Posted, Reversed, etc.) | | **POSTED BY** | Name and email of the user who posted the entry | ### Example Entries of a Mature Account | Journal ID | Date | Description | Status | Posted By | |------------|------|-------------|--------|-----------| | `JE-2026-08-00219`
MANUAL | 31 Aug 2026
03:42 PM | Return Purchase | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00218`
MANUAL | 31 Aug 2026
03:28 PM | Returned Purchase | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00217`
MANUAL | 31 Aug 2026
03:19 PM | Advance Amount To Supplier | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00216`
MANUAL | 31 Aug 2026
03:10 PM | Purchase Drugs | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00212`
MANUAL | 31 Aug 2026
12:41 PM | Purchased Drugs | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00210`
MANUAL | 31 Aug 2026
12:25 PM | Medicine Inventory | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00208`
AUTO PURCHASE | 31 Aug 2026
11:34 AM | Purchase 2026/124 From Aleeza | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00206`
AUTO PURCHASE REVERSAL | 31 Aug 2026
11:33 AM | Purchase Was Updated | REVERSAL | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00207`
AUTO PURCHASE | 31 Aug 2026
11:33 AM | Edit Purchase From 2026/123 To Aleeza | POSTED | Mujtabaa | | `JE-2026-08-00205`
AUTO PURCHASE | 31 Aug 2026
11:32 AM | Purchase 2026/123 From Aleeza | REVERSED | Mujtabaa | ![MediFlux Auto-Generated and Reversed Journal Entries](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/0c4f7562-f89d-4dcd-a110-0d95d91b27f7-journal-entries.png) *Caption: Purchase-related pharmacy journals showing POSTED, REVERSAL, and REVERSED statuses in MediFlux.* --- ## Newly Initialized Stores When you first set up accounting, MediFlux creates a single journal entry: - **Journal ID**: something like `JE-2026-08-00004` - **Type**: **ACCOUNTING INITIALIZATION** - **Description**: Entries Added On Initialization Of Chart Of Accounts - **Status**: POSTED This is normal. As you start recording sales, purchases, and manual journals, more entries will appear in the list. ![MediFlux Newly Initialized Store Journal Entry](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/d9ff3887-9dd9-4dc8-9660-ed86377ef303-new-journal.png) *Caption: The single Accounting Initialization journal shown on a newly set-up MediFlux pharmacy store.* --- ## Common Mistakes > **[Warning: Looking at the wrong date range]** The list defaults to the **current month**. If you expect to see older entries and the list looks empty, open the date range picker and select a wider period or **Last Month**. > **[Warning: Confusing REVERSED and REVERSAL]** **REVERSED** means the original entry has been cancelled by a later reversal entry. **REVERSAL** is the status of the entry that performed the reversal. Both appear in the list so you have a complete audit trail. --- ## Frequently Asked Questions ### Can I edit a posted journal entry? Posted journal entries cannot be edited directly. If a correction is needed, create a new reversing entry or use the appropriate adjustment workflow (for example, editing a purchase will automatically generate a reversal and a new entry). ### Why do some descriptions appear as links? Descriptions that come from purchases or other linked documents are clickable. Clicking them opens the related purchase or document so you can see the full details. ### What is the difference between MANUAL and AUTO PURCHASE? **MANUAL** entries are created by you using **Add Journal**. **AUTO PURCHASE** (and **AUTO PURCHASE REVERSAL**) entries are generated automatically by MediFlux whenever a purchase is recorded, edited, or reversed. ### How do I export the list for my accountant? Click **Export** and choose PDF or Excel. The export respects the current search and filter settings, so only the entries you are viewing are included. --- ## Next Steps * [Add Journal Entry](/docs/accounting/add-journal-entry) - Create a manual debit and credit entry using your Chart of Accounts. * [Chart of Accounts](/docs/accounting/ledger.md) - Browse the full list of accounts used in journal entries. * [General Ledger](/docs/accounting/ledger) - View the running balance and full history of any individual account. * [Trial Balance](/docs/accounting/trial-balance) - Check that total debits equal total credits across all accounts.

docs/accounting/ledger.title: Ledgers
docs/accounting/ledger.description: Manage your pharmacy chart of accounts in MediFlux. Track ledgers for assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, and expenses easily.
docs/accounting/ledger.body:
# Ledgers

## What Are Ledgers

In MediFlux, **Ledgers** are the individual accounts that make up your **pharmacy's Chart of Accounts**. Each ledger tracks a specific category of financial activity—from cash in your bank to money owed by customers, from sales revenue to monthly rent. Every transaction you record posts to at least two ledgers, keeping your books balanced automatically.

---

## Open Your Chart of Accounts

Go to **Accounting → Ledgers** from the left sidebar. You will see your full Chart of Accounts with all parent groups collapsed by default.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Chart of Accounts (Ledgers) Overview](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/3c9f9d0f-79cd-4c9e-9343-0cfb0692ed1a-ledger-overview.png)
*Caption: Ledgers page showing the complete pharmacy Chart of Accounts with all parent groups collapsed in MediFlux.*

---

## Find and Filter Accounts

Use **Search Ledgers** at the top to find any account by name instantly.

![MediFlux Search Pharmacy Ledgers](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/123e891b-ae26-441c-9d4a-9f97ece3088f-search_ledger.png)
*Caption: Search bar to instantly find a specific pharmacy ledger account by name in MediFlux.*

Below the search bar, five filter cards let you narrow the table to a specific account group. Click any card to show only accounts from that group:

| Card | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Liability** | All current and non-current liability accounts |
| **Assets** | All current and non-current asset accounts |
| **Equity** | Owner capital, drawings, retained earnings, and current year earnings |
| **Revenue** | Sales revenue, other income, and service income accounts |
| **Expenses** | COGS, indirect expenses, and other operating expenses |

Click the same card again to clear the filter and return to the full list.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Ledger Filter Cards](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/5b6700ed-0129-4edb-a104-11303c5cae07-filter-bars.png)
*Caption: Filter cards active, showing only equity accounts in the MediFlux pharmacy Chart of Accounts.*

---

## Browse the Accounts Table

The main table lists every ledger in a nested tree. Parent groups (like **Cash & Bank** or **Inventory**) show folder icons and can be expanded to reveal their child accounts. Leaf-level accounts show document icons.

| Column | What it means |
|--------|---------------|
| **Ledger** | Account name with a `Dr` or `Cr` badge showing its normal balance. Folder icons indicate parent groups. Document icons indicate leaf-level accounts |
| **Type** | Color-coded tag such as `CURRENT ASSET`, `CURRENT LIABILITY`, `EQUITY`, `REVENUE`, `EXPENSE`, `NON CURRENT ASSET`, or `NON CURRENT LIABILITY` |
| **Description** | A short explanation of what the account tracks |

> **What is Normal Balance?** In double-entry accounting, every account type has a normal balance—the side (debit or credit) on which the account naturally increases. Assets and expenses normally increase on the debit side (`Dr`). Liabilities, equity, and revenue normally increase on the credit side (`Cr`). The `Dr`/`Cr` badge in the UI shows this normal balance.

Click the **arrow icon** at the far right of any row to jump directly to that account's **General Ledger**. This opens a dedicated report showing every transaction posted to that ledger, with running balances and date filters.

---

## Edit Chart of Accounts

Click **+ Edit** at the top of the Ledgers page to open the **Setup Chart of Accounts** screen. This is where you control which accounts are active and can edit account names or descriptions.

![MediFlux Edit Pharmacy Chart of Accounts](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/3bf9b853-8613-4895-886b-9a67d4c3f825-edit-button.png)
*Caption: Click + Edit on the Ledgers page to open the screen to select accounts and manage the nested tree in MediFlux.*

### What You Can Do on This Screen

- **Add new accounts** using the **ADD NEW ACCOUNTS** section at the top (for example, add Owner capital).
- Expand parent groups to see child accounts.
- Check or uncheck accounts to include or exclude them from your Chart of Accounts.
- Accounts marked with a red asterisk (`*`) are required and cannot be unchecked.
- Click **Update** in the top-right to save your changes.

### Edit an Account Name or Description

Click the **pencil (edit) icon** on the right side of any account row. The **Edit Custom Account** dialog opens.

![MediFlux Edit Custom Pharmacy Ledger Account](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/f531316f-4daf-4c71-bfd8-5235d71bdd67-edit-dialog.png)
*Caption: Dialog to change the Account Name and Description for a custom pharmacy ledger in MediFlux.*

In this dialog you can:

- Change the **Account Name**
- Update the **Description**

Other fields (Account Type, Account Side, Parent Account, Contra) are shown for reference. After making changes, click **Update Account** to save.

Click **Cancel** or the **X** to close without saving.

---

## Account Breakdown

The following sections list every parent group and its child accounts. **Parent groups that contain further sub-groups are shown in bold.** Use these tables as a quick reference to understand what each ledger tracks and where your transactions post.

### Assets

Assets are what your pharmacy owns. They are split into **Current Assets** (convertible to cash within a year) and **Non-Current Assets** (long-term holdings).

#### Current Assets

| Account | Normal Balance | Type | Tracks |
|---------|----------------|------|--------|
| **Accounts Receivable** | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Amounts customers owe to the pharmacy |
| Customer Receivables | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Outstanding credit bills from customers |
| Other Receivables | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Any other money owed to the store |
| **Cash & Bank** | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | All cash, bank, and wallet balances |
| **Bank Accounts** | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Money held in bank accounts |
|   <small>└─ Test Bank</small> | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | <small>Individual bank account (shows bank details in description)</small> |
| Cash on Hand | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Physical cash held at the store |
| Digital Wallets | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Balances in UPI, wallets, and payment gateways |
| **Inventory** | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Value of all stock held for sale |
| Medicine Inventory | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | All pharmaceutical items in stock |
| Non-Drug Inventory | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | OTC goods, cosmetics, and FMCG items |
| Purchase Return | `Cr` | CURRENT ASSET | Value of medicines returned to suppliers |
| Purchase Return - Non-Drug Inventory | `Cr` | CURRENT ASSET | Value of non-drug inventory returned to suppliers |
| **Prepaid Expenses** | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Advance payments made by the store |
| Staff Advances | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Loans or advances given to staff |
| Supplier Advances | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Advance amounts paid to suppliers |
| **Tax Assets** | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | Input GST balances claimable |
| GST Input CGST | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | CGST paid that can be claimed as credit |
| GST Input IGST | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | IGST paid that can be claimed as credit |
| GST Input SGST | `Dr` | CURRENT ASSET | SGST paid that can be claimed as credit |

![MediFlux Pharmacy Current Assets Ledgers](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/afb9c3fe-b905-4f81-825d-256469ec96d8-current-assests.png)
*Caption: Expanded view of nested child accounts under Current Assets in the MediFlux pharmacy Chart of Accounts.*

#### Non-Current Assets

| Account | Normal Balance | Type | Tracks |
|---------|----------------|------|--------|
| **Deposits** | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Refundable deposits paid by the store |
| Security Deposits | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Deposits with landlords or service providers |
| Utility Deposits | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Deposits paid to utility companies |
| **Fixed Assets** | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Long-term assets used in store operations |
| Accumulated Depreciation | `Cr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | The value of assets that has been used up over time |
| Equipment | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Computers, printers, barcode scanners, air conditioning |
| Furniture & Fixtures | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Shelves, counters, racks, and furniture |
| Leasehold Improvements | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Renovations or improvements to rented space |
| Property/Building | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | The building you own |
| Vehicles | `Dr` | NON CURRENT ASSET | Delivery vehicles |

> **Note:** `Accumulated Depreciation` carries a `Cr` balance because it is a **contra-asset** account. It reduces the book value of your fixed assets over time rather than adding to them.

---

### Liabilities

Liabilities are what your pharmacy owes to others. They are split into **Current Liabilities** (due within a year) and **Non-Current Liabilities** (due after more than one year).

#### Current Liabilities

| Account | Normal Balance | Type | Tracks |
|---------|----------------|------|--------|
| **Accounts Payable** | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Amounts owed to suppliers for inventory and expenses |
| Non-Inventory Payables | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Payables for non-stock expenses like rent or utilities |
| Trade Creditors | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Outstanding amounts due to product suppliers |
| **Accrued Expenses** | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Expenses incurred but not yet paid |
| Accrued Salaries | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Employee salaries due but unpaid |
| Accrued Utilities | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Electricity, water, and internet charges due but unpaid |
| **GST Payable** | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | GST collected on sales and owed to the government |
| GST Adjustment | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Temporary GST adjustments and rounding differences |
| **Output GST** | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | GST collected from customers during sales |
|   <small>├─ GST Output CGST</small> | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | <small>Central GST collected from customers</small> |
|   <small>├─ GST Output IGST</small> | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | <small>Integrated GST collected from customers</small> |
|   <small>└─ GST Output SGST</small> | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | <small>State GST collected from customers</small> |
| **Short-Term Liabilities** | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Loans and obligations due within one year |
| Credit Card Payable | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Outstanding business credit card balance |
| Short-Term Loan | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Bank loan instalments due within the current year |
| **Statutory Liabilities** | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Taxes collected or deducted but not yet remitted |
| TCS Payable | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Tax collected at source and to be deposited |
| TDS Payable | `Cr` | CURRENT LIABILITY | Tax deducted at source and owed to the government |

![MediFlux Pharmacy Current Liabilities Ledgers](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/1b8ef3c2-3341-42f1-9b64-58083684908f-liabilities.png)
*Caption: Expanded view of nested child accounts under Current Liabilities in the MediFlux pharmacy Chart of Accounts.*

#### Non-Current Liabilities

| Account | Normal Balance | Type | Tracks |
|---------|----------------|------|--------|
| **Long-Term Liabilities** | `Cr` | NON CURRENT LIABILITY | Financial obligations due after more than one year |
| Long-Term Loan | `Cr` | NON CURRENT LIABILITY | Bank loans repayable over more than one year |
| Mortgage Loan | `Cr` | NON CURRENT LIABILITY | Long-term building or property loan |

---

### Equity

Equity represents the owner's stake in the business. These accounts track capital invested, drawings taken, and profits retained.

| Account | Normal Balance | Type | Tracks |
|---------|----------------|------|--------|
| **Equity** | `Cr` | EQUITY | Owner's total stake in the business after liabilities |
| Additional Paid-In Capital | `Cr` | EQUITY | Any extra capital invested by owners beyond the initial investment |
| Current Year Earnings (Calculated) | `Cr` | EQUITY | Profit or loss generated in the ongoing accounting period |
| **Mehreen Aijaz** | `Cr` | EQUITY | Partner account group |
|   <small>├─ Owner's Capital - Mehreen Aijaz</small> | `Cr` | EQUITY | <small>Capital account for the partner</small> |
|   <small>├─ Owner's Drawings - Mehreen Aijaz</small> | `Dr` | EQUITY | <small>Drawing account for the partner</small> |
|   <small>└─ Partner Remuneration - Mehreen Aijaz</small> | `Dr` | EXPENSE | <small>Remuneration paid to the partner for services</small> |
| Opening Balance equity | `Cr` | EQUITY | Temporary equity account used to record the net difference during setup |
| Retained Earnings | `Cr` | EQUITY | Accumulated profits kept in the business from previous years |

> **Note:** `Mehreen Aijaz` is shown here as an example partner account. In your system, you will see the name of the partner or owner you configured during setup.
>
> `Current Year Earnings (Calculated)` is highlighted in the table because it is auto-computed by MediFlux. It aggregates all revenue and expense transactions for the current accounting period. You cannot post manual journal entries to it.
>
> `Partner Remuneration` sits under the **Equity** parent but is tagged as `EXPENSE` because it represents an operating cost paid to the partner for services rendered.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Equity and Partner Ledgers](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/09/d3837fa9-0cd2-42ed-8c6c-d225696be344-equity.png)
*Caption: Expanded view of partner capital, drawings, and retained earnings in the MediFlux pharmacy Chart of Accounts.*

---

### Revenue

Revenue accounts track all income earned by the pharmacy.

| Account | Normal Balance | Type | Tracks |
|---------|----------------|------|--------|
| **Revenue** | `Cr` | REVENUE | Total income earned from pharmacy sales and services |
| **Other Income** | `Cr` | REVENUE | Non-sales income such as bank interest and supplier discounts |
|   <small>├─ Bank Interest</small> | `Cr` | REVENUE | <small>Interest income earned on bank balances and fixed deposits</small> |
|   <small>├─ Customer Adjustment Income</small> | `Cr` | REVENUE | <small>Income recognized from customer account adjustments</small> |
|   <small>├─ Customer Credit Write-off</small> | `Cr` | REVENUE | <small>Income recognized when customer credit balances are written off</small> |
|   <small>├─ Round Off Gain</small> | `Cr` | REVENUE | <small>Gain arising due to rounding off invoice totals</small> |
|   <small>├─ Supplier Adjustment Income</small> | `Cr` | REVENUE | <small>Income recognized from supplier account adjustments</small> |
|   <small>└─ Supplier Waive-off & Adjustments</small> | `Cr` | REVENUE | <small>Income recognized when supplier dues or payable balances are waived</small> |
| **Sales Revenue** | `Cr` | REVENUE | Primary income from selling medicines - retail and wholesale |
|   <small>├─ Retail Sales</small> | `Cr` | REVENUE | <small>Revenue from selling medicines directly to customers</small> |
|   <small>├─ Retail Sales discount</small> | `Dr` | REVENUE | <small>Customer discount reducing total revenue</small> |
