  * [Add Purchase](/docs/purchases/add-purchase) - Record a new purchase bill when fresh stock arrives.
  * [Drug List](/docs/inventory/drug-list) - Check how your inventory looks after recent purchases.
  * [Supplier Ledger](/docs/supplier/supplier-ledger) - See what you still owe suppliers for unpaid purchases.
  * [Purchase Orders](/docs/purchases/purchase-orders) - Raise orders for stock you haven't received yet.

docs/purchases/trash.title: Purchase Trash
docs/purchases/trash.description: View, restore, or permanently review purchases that have been deleted.
docs/purchases/trash.body:
# Purchase Trash

The **Trash** page holds every purchase that has been deleted from your pharmacy's records. Deleted purchases stay here until restored, giving you a safety net for accidental deletions.

---

## Searching Deleted Purchases
The search bar at the top lets you search across **suppliers, drugs, and challan numbers**. To the left of the search bar, the **All** dropdown lets you narrow the search scope, similar to the [Purchase List](/docs/purchases/purchase-list) page.

![Search Deleted Purchases](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/07/e7f9f13c-9152-4536-ae23-7b41f098ac07-trash-purchase-search.png)
*Caption: Search across suppliers, drugs, and challan numbers to find deleted purchases.*

---

## The Trash List
Each entry in the list shows:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Purchase number** | The original purchase number, with an **Unpaid** tag where relevant |
| **Supplier** | Name of the supplier the purchase was made from |
| **Deleted** | Tag confirming the purchase is deleted, along with the date and time it was deleted |
| **Items** | Number of items and total value of the purchase |
| **Actions** | Quick action menu for that entry |

The page shows a **Found X** count above the list indicating how many deleted purchases match your search.

Every entry is shown expanded by default, with the full line item breakdown visible below it:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **SR.** | Serial number of the line item |
| **HSN** | HSN code of the drug |
| **Product** | Name of the drug |
| **Batch** | Batch number |
| **Expiry** | Expiry date of the batch |
| **QTY** | Quantity purchased |
| **Purchase Price** | Price paid per unit at the time of purchase |

The **Grand Total** for that purchase is shown at the bottom right. Click the **chevron** on the right of an entry to collapse or expand its line items.

![Trash List](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/07/2f5fa503-8079-4ae0-8ba0-b9f67c483a29-trash-purchase.png)
*Caption: Deleted purchases with expanded line items, supplier details, and restore options.*

---

## Row Actions
Clicking the **three-dot menu (⋮)** on any entry opens a quick-actions menu with two options:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **View Details** | Opens the full details for this deleted purchase |
| **Restore** | Restores the purchase back to the active Purchase List |

![Trash Actions](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/07/dfd63c27-033a-4fb1-bf2e-229c890cae45-row-actionss.png)
*Caption: View details or restore a deleted purchase from the actions menu.*

---

## When There Are No Deleted Purchases
If nothing matches your search, or Trash is empty, the page shows a **"No Deleted Purchases Found"** message along with a **Reset Filters** button to clear your search and start over.

![Empty Trash](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/07/9d354638-ff28-448f-b0f3-64cc5d4af4a6-empty-trash.png)
*Caption: No deleted purchases found, use Reset Filters to clear your search.*

---

## Recover What You Need
Restored your purchases? Here's where to go next.


  * [Purchase List](/docs/purchases/purchase-list) - Verify restored purchases are back in your active records.
  * [Add Purchase](/docs/purchases/add-purchase) - Record new purchases and avoid future deletions with accurate entry.
  * [Drug List](/docs/inventory/drug-list) - Check that restored purchase stock is reflected in inventory.
  * [Supplier Ledger](/docs/supplier/supplier-ledger) - Confirm restored purchases updated supplier payables correctly.

docs/reports/creditors-debtors.title: Creditors / Debtors
docs/reports/creditors-debtors.description: View customer and supplier balances, filter outstanding ledgers, and export creditors and debtors reports in MediFlux.
docs/reports/creditors-debtors.body:
# Creditors / Debtors

The **Creditors / Debtors** report provides an overview of outstanding balances across your customers, suppliers, and general ledgers. It helps you identify amounts payable or receivable, review customer advances, and understand your store's overall credit and debit position.

You can search for specific ledgers, filter balances by category, include or exclude general ledgers, and export the report with your preferred columns and sorting options.

To review individual transactions and payments, see [Customer Ledger](/docs/customers/customer-ledger), [Supplier Ledger](/docs/supplier/supplier-ledger), and [General Ledger](/docs/accounting/general-ledger).

## Opening the Creditors / Debtors Report



### Open Reports

From the MediFlux sidebar, expand **Reports**.

### Select Creditors/Debtors

Click **Creditors/Debtors** to open the report.

### Review the Report

The page displays three balance summaries followed by a detailed table of individual ledger balances.



![Creditors / Debtors Report](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/1bf687e8-285b-4698-a3c7-a75e26064a10-creditor-debtors.png)
*Caption: The Creditors / Debtors page displays credit and debit summaries, search and filter controls, and individual ledger balances.*

## Understanding the Summary Cards

The report displays three summary sections at the top.

| Section | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Total Credit** | Combined credit balances of the included ledgers. |
| **Total Debit** | Combined debit balances of the included ledgers. |
| **Net Position** | Difference between total credit and total debit, indicating whether the report has a net credit or debit excess. |

The summary also displays applicable balance categories, such as:

- **Supplier Payables:** Outstanding credit balances associated with suppliers.
- **Customer Advances:** Credit balances held against customers.

![Credit and Debit Summary](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/5c5d109a-2f10-4fcc-b89c-73e12663e803-summary.png)
*Caption: The summary cards display Total Credit, Total Debit, and Net Position, with applicable breakdowns such as Supplier Payables and Customer Advances.*

> **[Note]** The displayed amounts depend on the ledger categories and general ledger settings selected in the report.

## Searching and Filtering Ledgers

The controls above the summary allow you to narrow the report to the balances you want to review.

### Search for a Ledger

Use the **Search by ledger, area...** field to find a customer, supplier, ledger, or area.

### Filter by Ledger Category

Click **All Ledgers** to open the **Includes Filters (Multi-Select)** dropdown.

The available options include:

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **All Ledgers** | Includes suppliers, customers, and general ledger entries. |
| **Creditors** | Shows ledgers with credit balances. |
| **Debtors** | Shows ledgers with debit balances. |
| **Trade Payables** | Includes supplier payables and payable general ledger accounts. |
| **Trade Receivables** | Includes customer receivables and receivable general ledger accounts. |

You can select multiple categories using the checkboxes.

![Ledger Category Filters](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/e43d74c1-ec10-498b-bfa1-5c5ef76b0a8a-ledger-filters.png)
*Caption: The multi-select dropdown lets you choose All Ledgers, Creditors, Debtors, Trade Payables, and Trade Receivables.*

### Include or Exclude General Ledgers

Use the **GL: Include** dropdown to control whether general ledger accounts are included.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **GL: Include** | Includes applicable general ledger accounts in the report. |
| **GL: Exclude** | Excludes general ledger accounts from the report. |

![General Ledger Inclusion Filter](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/c5a26c57-faf9-4931-bebc-1665df144973-L-filter.png)
*Caption: Choose GL: Include or GL: Exclude to control whether general ledger accounts appear in the Creditors / Debtors report.*

## Understanding the Ledger Table

The table below the summary displays the individual balances of the included ledgers.

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **#** | Serial number of the ledger entry. |
| **Ledger** | Ledger name, with its type displayed below where applicable. |
| **Debit** | Debit balance associated with the ledger. |
| **Credit** | Credit balance associated with the ledger. |

The **TOTAL** row at the bottom displays the combined debit and credit amounts.

![Creditors / Debtors Ledger Table](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/16a13d00-9850-44da-b143-343f38e5cb9b-ledger-table.png)
*Caption: The table lists individual ledgers with their debit or credit balances and a total row.*

> **[Note]** A dash (`—`) indicates that no amount is displayed in that balance column for the corresponding ledger.

## Exporting the Creditors / Debtors Report

You can customize the information included in the exported report.



### Click Export

Click **Export** in the upper-right corner of the Creditors / Debtors page.

The **Export Creditors / Debtors** dialog opens.

### Choose the Columns

Under **Columns to include**, select the columns you want in the exported report.

The available columns are:

- **Ledger**
- **Debit**
- **Credit**

The **Ledger** column is locked and remains included.

### Select the Ledger Categories

Use the **Include** dropdown to choose which ledger categories should appear in the export.

### Set General Ledger Inclusion

Use **GL Include** to include or exclude general ledger accounts.

### Choose Sorting Options

Use **Sort by** to select the field used for sorting and **Order** to choose the sorting direction.

For example, you can sort by **Ledger** in **A–Z** order.

### Export the Report

Click **Export** to proceed with the selected settings.



![Export Creditors / Debtors](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/2a74bcfe-c30d-4205-b152-60cee83803ee-export.png)
*Caption: Customize the export by selecting columns, ledger categories, general ledger inclusion, sorting field, and order before exporting.*

## When to Use This Report

The Creditors / Debtors report is useful when you need to:

- Review outstanding supplier payables.
- Identify customer debit and credit balances.
- Check customer advances.
- View trade payables and receivables separately.
- Compare overall credit and debit positions.
- Export balances for accounting review or reconciliation.

> **[Note]** To examine the transactions behind an individual balance, refer to the corresponding customer or supplier ledger.

docs/reports/gst-return.title: GST Returns
docs/reports/gst-return.description: Generate pharmacy GST returns in MediFlux. Easily configure GSTR-1, GSTR-2, and GSTR-3B reports, select periods, and ensure tax compliance.
docs/reports/gst-return.body:
# GST Returns

The **GST Returns & Compliance** page helps you prepare and review **pharmacy GST reports** using your store's transaction data in **MediFlux**.

You can select a GST return type, choose a reporting period, and generate reports for review. For supported return types, you can also select which sections to include.

To review the transactions used in these reports, see [Sales List](/docs/sales/sale-list) and [Purchase List](/docs/purchases/purchase-list).

## Opening GST Returns & Compliance

1. **Open Reports**

   From the MediFlux sidebar, expand **Reports**.

2. **Select GST Returns**

   Click **GST Returns** to open the **GST Returns & Compliance** page.

3. **Choose a Return Type**

   Select the GST return you want to prepare from the tabs at the top of the page.

![MediFlux Pharmacy GST Returns & Compliance Page](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/5d8678e5-222c-4653-83d0-e363c1438b0b-gst-reports.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux GST Returns page displaying return tabs, reporting parameters, and section-selection controls for pharmacy tax compliance.*

## Available GST Return Types

The page displays four return tabs.

| Return | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **GSTR-1** | Review outward supply and sales-related GST information. |
| **GSTR-2** | Review purchase-related GST information. |
| **GSTR-3B** | Prepare a summary of GST-related information for the selected reporting period. |
| **GSTR-9** | Annual GST return option, currently disabled in the interface. |

> **[Note]** **GSTR-9** is displayed as a disabled tab and cannot currently be selected from this page.

## Configuring Report Parameters

The **Report Parameters** section allows you to choose the period for which you want to generate the GST report.

The same parameter controls are visible for GSTR-1, GSTR-2, and GSTR-3B.

### Frequency

Use the **Frequency** dropdown to select the reporting frequency.

The available options are:

- **Monthly**
- **Quarterly**
- **Annually**

![MediFlux GST Report Frequency Selection](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/300e55f7-c758-4394-b6c1-be9e19e6388f-frequency.png)
*Caption: Choose Monthly, Quarterly, or Annually from the Frequency dropdown for pharmacy GST reports in MediFlux.*

### Financial Year

Use **Financial Year** to choose the year for which you want to prepare the report.

For example, the screenshot shows the following available years:

- `2026-2027`
- `2025-2026`
- `2024-2025`
- `2023-2024`

![MediFlux GST Financial Year Selection](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/6238e0b9-e39f-48d7-976c-5e61633f976c-financial-year.png)
*Caption: Choose the financial year for which the pharmacy GST report should be generated in MediFlux.*

### Select Month

When using the monthly reporting view, use **Select Month** to choose the required month.

For example, you can select **October** for the financial year `2026-2027`.

![MediFlux GST Reporting Month Selection](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/9e3f6723-8d12-4eb2-afd6-5f4dac5fdcb2-select-month.png)
*Caption: Choose the specific month for which you want to fetch pharmacy GST report data in MediFlux.*

> **[Note]** The screenshots show the month selector for **Monthly** frequency. The period-selection behavior for **Quarterly** and **Annually** follows a similar pattern.

## Generating GSTR-1

**GSTR-1** provides outward-supply information organized into GST reporting sections.

1. **Select GSTR-1**

   Click the **GSTR-1** tab.

2. **Configure the Reporting Period**

   Choose the **Frequency**, **Financial Year**, and applicable reporting month.

3. **Select the Sections**

   Use the **Sections** panel to choose which parts of the report to include.

4. **Fetch the Report**

   Click **Fetch Report** to request the report for the selected period and sections.

### GSTR-1 Sections

The following sections are available in the interface:

| Section | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **B2B Invoices** | Transactions involving registered taxpayers. |
| **B2C Small** | Retail transactions. |
| **B2C Large** | High-value interstate transactions. |
| **HSN Summary** | Drug-wise aggregation for HSN reporting. |
| **CDNR** | Credit and debit notes for registered taxpayers. |
| **CDNUR** | Credit and debit notes for unregistered taxpayers. |
| **Documents Issued** | Document details associated with Table 13. |

Each section has a checkbox that allows you to include or exclude it.

You can also click **Deselect All** to clear the selected sections.

![MediFlux GSTR-1 Report Sections for Pharmacy](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/132f7ff6-6fbf-4a53-b37b-ff197ce5c3ce-gstr-1.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux GSTR-1 Sections panel includes B2B Invoices, B2C Small, B2C Large, HSN Summary, CDNR, CDNUR, and Documents Issued.*

## Generating GSTR-2

The **GSTR-2** tab provides purchase-related reporting options.

1. **Select GSTR-2**

   Click the **GSTR-2** tab.

2. **Choose the Reporting Period**

   Select the **Frequency**, **Financial Year**, and applicable month.

3. **Select the Required Sections**

   Choose the sections to include in the report.

4. **Fetch the Report**

   Click **Fetch Report**.

### GSTR-2 Sections

The interface displays the following options:

| Section | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **B2B Invoices** | Purchase invoices involving registered taxpayers. |
| **B2B Unregistered** | Transactions involving unregistered taxpayers. |
| **CDNR** | Credit and debit notes for registered taxpayers. |
| **CDNUR** | Credit and debit notes for unregistered taxpayers. |

![MediFlux GSTR-2 Report Configuration for Pharmacy](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/a52a6a65-93d8-4975-bbfb-15553f587bf4-gstr-2.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux GSTR-2 tab displays reporting parameters and section checkboxes for B2B Invoices, B2B Unregistered, CDNR, and CDNUR.*

> **[Note]** The **Sections** panel is different for GSTR-1 and GSTR-2. Select the relevant return tab before choosing sections.

## Generating GSTR-3B

The **GSTR-3B** tab provides a GST summary reporting view.

Unlike GSTR-1 and GSTR-2, the GSTR-3B screen shown here does not display a separate **Sections** panel.

1. **Select GSTR-3B**

   Click the **GSTR-3B** tab.

2. **Configure the Period**

   Choose the reporting **Frequency**, **Financial Year**, and applicable month.

3. **Fetch the Report**

   Click **Fetch Report** to request the GSTR-3B report for the selected period.

![MediFlux GSTR-3B Report Configuration for Pharmacy](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/c6be86c9-cb30-4e86-8e72-2795ade2c424-gstr-3.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux GSTR-3B tab displays reporting frequency, financial year, month selection, and the Fetch Report button.*

## Selecting and Deselecting Report Sections

For GSTR-1 and GSTR-2, the **Sections** panel determines which categories are included when fetching the report.

To customize the selection:

1. Open the required GST return tab.
2. Locate the **Sections** panel.
3. Use the checkboxes to select or deselect individual sections.
4. Click **Deselect All** if you want to clear the current selection.
5. Select the required sections and click **Fetch Report**.

## Important Things to Check

Before using GST report data for filing or reconciliation, review the following:

- Confirm that the correct **Financial Year** and reporting period are selected.
- Check that the required report sections are included.
- Review purchase and sales transactions for missing or incorrect GST details.
- Verify applicable GST rates, HSN codes, and invoice information.
- Reconcile the generated figures with your accounting records and relevant GST portal data.

> **[Warning]** Generating a GST report in MediFlux does not, by itself, mean that a GST return has been filed with the government. Review and reconcile the information before using it for statutory filing.

## FAQs

  ### Can I generate GST reports for previous financial years?

Yes. Use the **Financial Year** dropdown to select an available previous financial year.

  ### Can I choose which sections to include in GSTR-1?

Yes. The **Sections** panel allows you to select or deselect individual sections before clicking **Fetch Report**.

  ### Are the sections in GSTR-1 and GSTR-2 the same?

No. GSTR-1 and GSTR-2 have different section options. The available sections change based on the selected return type.

  ### Can I generate GSTR-3B without selecting sections?

Yes. The GSTR-3B page does not display a separate **Sections** panel. Select the reporting period and click **Fetch Report**.

  ### Can I access GSTR-9?

No. The **GSTR-9** tab is currently disabled.

  ### Does generating a GST report automatically file my return?

No. Generating a report in MediFlux does not automatically file it with the GST portal. Review and reconcile the report before filing.

docs/reports/overview.title: Reports
docs/reports/overview.description: Explore MediFlux reports to monitor stock, track outstanding balances, and review GST-related business data.
docs/reports/overview.body:
# Reports

The **Reports** section in MediFlux helps you review important business information in one place. From monitoring inventory and outstanding payments to reviewing GST-related records, these reports make it easier to understand your pharmacy's operations and keep track of business activity.

Each report focuses on a specific area of your business, allowing you to find the information you need without going through individual transactions.

## Explore Reports

Choose a report category to view detailed information and learn how to use it.


  * [Stock Reports](/docs/reports/stock-reports) - Review medicine stock, monitor inventory movement, and access stock-related information.

  * [Creditors & Debtors](/docs/reports/creditors-debtors) - Review outstanding amounts payable to suppliers and receivable from customers.

  * [GST Returns](/docs/reports/gst-return) - Access GST-related reports and review tax information for your business.


---

## Why Use Reports?

Reports help you understand different aspects of your pharmacy's operations.

| Area | What You Can Review |
| --- | --- |
| **Inventory** | Stock information and medicine inventory activity |
| **Outstanding Balances** | Amounts receivable from customers and payable to suppliers |
| **GST** | Tax-related information required for reviewing business records |

Instead of checking individual sales, purchases, or inventory entries, you can use the relevant report to review information for that part of your business.

---

## More Reports

MediFlux continues to expand its reporting capabilities. As additional reports become available, they will be included in this section with dedicated guides explaining their purpose and how to use them.

> **[Note]** Select any report from the **Explore Reports** section to learn about its available options, filters, and how to interpret the information it provides.

docs/reports/stock-reports.title: Stock Reports
docs/reports/stock-reports.description: Learn how to view stock movements, check inventory levels, identify ageing and expiring medicines, and generate customized stock reports in MediFlux.
docs/reports/stock-reports.body:
# Stock Reports

## Stock Reports

The **Stock Reports** section in MediFlux helps you track inventory movements, review available stock, identify medicines that need attention, and understand the value of your inventory.

Whether you want to check today's stock movements, find medicines nearing expiry, identify products that are not selling, or calculate the value of your stock, you can generate the relevant report from one place.

MediFlux provides ready-to-use reports for common requirements, along with manual reports that let you customize how the information is grouped and displayed.

For inventory searching and filtering, see [Drug List](/docs/inventory/drug-list). To review stock across warehouses, see [Warehouse](/docs/inventory/warehouse).

## Accessing Stock Reports



### Open  Reports

From the left sidebar, expand **Reports**.

### Select Stock Reports

Click **Stock Reports** to open the report selection page.

### Choose a Report

Browse the available reports, search for a report by name, or select a report type to narrow the list.



![Stock Reports](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/e08760ec-ff88-4274-8a40-26189d48af6f-stock-reports.png)
*Caption: The Stock Reports page displays available report templates, a search bar, and a report type dropdown.*

By default, the page displays reports from **All types**.

## Finding a Report

With multiple reports available, you can use the search bar and report type dropdown to find the information you need.

### Search Reports

Use the **Search reports...** field to search for a report by its name.

For example, enter `Daily Stock Ledger`, `Near Expiry`, or `Stock Valuation` to find matching reports.

### Filter by Report Type

Click the **All types** dropdown at the top-right of the report list.

Select the category you want to explore.

The available report types are:

- **Stock Ledger**
- **Stock Register**
- **Stock Summary**
- **Stock Ageing**
- **Near Expiry**
- **Dead Stock**
- **Fast Moving**
- **Stock Valuation**

Selecting a category displays the reports belonging to that type. Choose **All types** to return to the complete list.

![Filter Reports by Type](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/8621217e-f553-48cb-826f-2b00a2215b06-report-filter.png)
*Caption: Use the report type dropdown to display reports from a particular stock report category.*

## Understanding Stock Report Types

Each report type serves a different purpose. Within a category, MediFlux provides several report templates for different periods, groupings, and analysis requirements.

### Stock Ledger

Stock Ledger reports show how inventory moves into and out of your store.

They help you trace stock movements through purchases, sales, returns, and other stock transactions.

Common reports include:

- **Daily Stock Ledger:** View individual stock movements for the day.
- **Stock Ledger (This Month):** Review item-level movements for the current month.
- **Purchase Ledger:** Review stock received through purchase vouchers.
- **Sales Ledger:** Review stock issued through sales.
- **Returns Ledger:** Track purchase and sales returns.
- **Batch-wise Ledger:** Review stock movements for individual batches.

You can also find reports grouped by warehouse, company, and medicine schedule.

**When to use:** Select Stock Ledger when you need to understand when, how, or through which transaction stock moved.

### Stock Register

Stock Register reports summarize stock movement over a selected period, including opening quantities, inward stock, outward stock, and closing quantities.

Available templates include:

- **Stock Register (This Month)**
- **Stock Register (Batch wise)**
- **Stock Register (Company wise)**
- **Stock Register (Category wise)**
- **Stock Register (Warehouse wise)**
- **Stock Register (HSN wise)**

You can also find reports for items with movement, items without movement, and stock quantities and values.

**When to use:** Select Stock Register when you want to reconcile opening stock, inward movement, outward movement, and closing stock.

### Stock Summary

Stock Summary reports provide an overview of available inventory.

You can review stock by medicine, batch, company, supplier, category, rack, warehouse, HSN code, and other groupings.

Examples include:

- **Stock Summary (Item wise):** Current stock for each medicine.
- **Stock Summary (Batch wise):** Stock details by batch, including MRP and expiry.
- **Out of Stock Items:** Medicines with zero stock.
- **Negative Stock Items:** Medicines with negative stock quantities.
- **Low Stock Items:** Medicines with stock greater than zero but at or below their reorder level.
- **High-Value Stock:** Available stock arranged by value.

**When to use:** Select Stock Summary to check stock availability, identify shortages, and review current inventory.

### Stock Ageing

Stock Ageing reports help you identify inventory that has remained in stock for longer periods.

They provide ageing information by item, batch, company, supplier, or warehouse.

Examples include:

- **Stock Ageing (Item wise)**
- **Ageing Bucket Matrix (Item wise)**
- **Stock older than 90 days**
- **Stock older than 180 days**
- **Stock Ageing (Batch wise)**
- **Ageing vs Last Month-end**

Ageing Bucket Matrix reports organize stock into age ranges such as `0–30`, `31–60`, `61–90`, `91–180`, and `180+` days.

**When to use:** Select Stock Ageing to identify older inventory and review stock that may require attention.

### Near Expiry

Near Expiry reports help you identify medicines that have expired or are approaching their expiry dates.

Examples include:

- **Near Expiry (Action List):** Expired stock and batches expiring within six months.
- **Expired Stock:** Stock that has already expired.
- **Expiring in 1 Month**
- **Expiring in 3 Months**
- **Returnable to Supplier:** Stock expiring within three to six months, grouped by supplier.
- **Expiry Bucket Summary:** Stock organized into expiry periods.

**When to use:** Select Near Expiry to plan stock returns, review expiry risks, and prioritize medicines that require action.

> **[Note]** The **Returnable to Supplier** report helps identify potentially returnable stock. Whether a supplier accepts a return depends on the supplier's return policy.

### Dead Stock

Dead Stock reports identify medicines that have not recorded sales during a particular period.

Available reports include:

- **Dead Stock (30 days)**
- **Dead Stock (60 days)**
- **Dead Stock (90 days)**
- **Dead Stock (180 days)**
- **Never Sold:** Purchased items that have never been sold.
- **Gone Cold:** Items that sold previously but have had no recent sales.
- **Staleness Summary:** Dead stock grouped by the time since its last sale.

You can also review dead stock by batch, supplier, company, or category.

**When to use:** Select Dead Stock to identify slow-selling inventory and make better purchasing and stock management decisions.

### Fast Moving

Fast Moving reports help you identify medicines with high sales activity.

Examples include:

- **Fast Moving (30 days)**
- **Fast Moving (60 days)**
- **Fast Moving (90 days)**
- **Fast Moving (180 days)**
- **Class A, B, and C Items**
- **ABC Summary**
- **Stockout Risk:** Fast-moving medicines with fewer estimated days of stock remaining.

Reports are also available by company and supplier.

**When to use:** Select Fast Moving to understand product demand, identify frequently sold medicines, and support replenishment planning.

### Stock Valuation

Stock Valuation reports help you understand the monetary value of your available inventory.

You can review stock value using different pricing bases, such as cost, MRP, or trade price.

Examples include:

- **Stock Valuation at Cost**
- **Stock Valuation at Cost (Company wise)**
- **Stock Valuation at MRP (Category wise)**
- **Stock Valuation (Batch wise)**
- **Potential Sales Value (at MRP)**
- **Margin Ranking (vs MRP)**
- **Valuation vs Last Month-end**
- **Stock Valuation (Manual)**

**When to use:** Select Stock Valuation to estimate inventory value, compare stock values, and review potential sales value.

> **[Note]** Stock valuation and potential sales value are different. A report calculated using MRP represents the value of stock at the listed maximum retail prices, not actual sales revenue.

## Generating a Predefined Report

Predefined reports come with settings for a particular purpose, such as today's stock ledger or medicines that have not sold in the last 90 days.

You can open these reports directly without manually selecting every parameter.

For example, to view the **Daily Stock Ledger**:



### Find the Report

Open **Stock Reports** and select **Stock Ledger** from the report type dropdown.

### Open Daily Stock Ledger

Click **Daily Stock Ledger**.

MediFlux opens the report using its predefined settings for today's stock movements.

### Review the Results

The report displays stock movements grouped by medicine, with transaction details and totals.



![Daily Stock Ledger](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/56a8fd5b-de58-476e-b27b-e8a4530bfef9-daily-stock-ledger.png)
*Caption: The Daily Stock Ledger displays stock movements grouped by medicine, with inward and outward quantities, balances, rates, and values.*

### Understanding the Daily Stock Ledger

The report contains columns such as:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Date | Date of the stock transaction |
| V.Type | Type of voucher, such as Sale |
| V.No. | Voucher number associated with the transaction |
| Party | Customer or other party associated with the voucher |
| Batch | Batch number of the medicine |
| In | Quantity added to stock |
| Out | Quantity removed from stock |
| Balance | Stock balance after the movement |
| Rate | Rate shown for the transaction |
| Value | Monetary value of the movement |

Medicine names appear as grouped rows.

Click the arrow beside a medicine to expand or collapse its transaction details.

The report also displays totals for the grouped records and a **Grand Total** at the bottom.

> **[Note]** A negative balance indicates that the calculated stock balance is below zero. Review the relevant transactions if the quantity does not match your physical stock.

## Generating a Manual Report

Manual reports allow you to select report settings before generating the results.

Each stock report category includes a manual option, such as **Stock Ledger (Manual)**, **Stock Register (Manual)**, or **Stock Valuation (Manual)**.

For example, to generate a customized Stock Valuation report:



### Select Stock Valuation

From the report type dropdown, select **Stock Valuation**.

### Open the Manual Report

Find and click **Stock Valuation (Manual)**.

### Configure the Report

A configuration dialog opens where you can select the required settings.

### Generate the Report

Click **Get Report** to generate the report using your selected configuration.



![Configure Stock Valuation Report](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/727c270a-da05-4e34-b0f5-b8cbddf76827-manual-report.png)
*Caption: The manual Stock Valuation report allows you to select table type, grouping, view, valuation basis, columns, and an as-of date.*

For Stock Valuation, the configuration shown includes:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Table Type | Choose how the report table is organized |
| Group By | Select how stock information is grouped |
| View | Choose the report view |
| Valuation Basis | Select the price basis used to calculate stock value |
| Select Columns | Choose which columns appear in the report |
| As-of Date | Select the date for which stock value should be calculated |

> **[Note]** The configuration workflow is available across stock report types. The settings displayed reflect the report being generated.

## Configuring an Open Report

You can also change report settings after opening a predefined report.

Click **Configure** above the report table to open its configuration dialog.

For example, the Stock Ledger configuration includes:

- **Primary Group:** Choose the main grouping for the report.
- **Secondary Group:** Choose how records are grouped within the primary group.
- **Analysis Dimension:** Select the inventory records to include.
- **Detail Level:** Choose the level of detail displayed.
- **Select Columns:** Select the columns to include in the report.
- **Date Period:** Choose the reporting period.

![Configure Stock Ledger Report](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/67bb7c58-429c-46e5-bbeb-ce8903ebe620-configure-report.png)
*Caption: The Configure dialog provides grouping, analysis, detail, column selection, and date period settings.*

After making your changes, click **Get Report**.

MediFlux generates the report according to the selected settings.

This allows you to start with a predefined report and adjust it when you need a different grouping, period, or level of detail.

## Filtering Report Results

Once a report is open, you can narrow the displayed information using **Filters**.



### Open Filters

Click **Filters** above the report table.

### Select Filter Values

Choose the required values from the available filter fields.

### Apply Filters

Click **Apply filters** to update the report results.



![Stock Report Filters](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/9c16d39a-524b-4ba6-813a-c8818bca230c-filter-report.png)
*Caption: The Filters panel allows users to narrow report results using customer, supplier, voucher, medicine, batch, warehouse, and manufacturer selections.*

The Stock Ledger filter panel includes:

| Filter | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Customers | Narrow results to selected customers |
| Suppliers | Narrow results to selected suppliers |
| Voucher Type | View transactions belonging to selected voucher types |
| Drugs | Limit results to selected medicines |
| Batch | View records for selected batches |
| Warehouse | Limit results to selected warehouses |
| Manufacturer | View records associated with selected manufacturers |

The available filtering options may depend on the report and its data.

## Searching Within a Report

Generated reports also provide a search field above the results table.

For example, the Stock Ledger displays **Search by primary or secondary grouping...**.

Use this field to locate matching groups within the report instead of scrolling through every record.

The search applies to the generated report, while the search field on the main Stock Reports page is used to find report templates.

## Exporting a Report

You can export a generated report for further review or recordkeeping.



### Open the Required Report

Select and generate the report you need.

### Review the Report

Apply any required configuration or filters and verify the results.

### Click Export

Click **Export** at the top-right of the report page.

### Complete the Export

Follow the available export options to save the report.



> **[Note]** Review the selected date period, grouping, and filters before exporting so that the report contains the information you intended to include.

## Choosing the Right Report

If you are unsure which report to use, start with the question you want to answer.

| What do you want to know? | Recommended report type |
| --- | --- |
| Which transactions increased or decreased stock? | Stock Ledger |
| What were the opening, inward, outward, and closing quantities? | Stock Register |
| How much stock is currently available? | Stock Summary |
| Which medicines have remained in stock for a long time? | Stock Ageing |
| Which medicines are expiring soon? | Near Expiry |
| Which medicines have not sold recently? | Dead Stock |
| Which medicines are selling the fastest? | Fast Moving |
| What is the monetary value of available stock? | Stock Valuation |

## Important Notes

- **All types** displays report templates from every stock report category.
- Selecting a report type filters the template list. It does not generate a report by itself.
- Predefined reports use settings appropriate to their stated purpose.
- Manual reports allow you to select report parameters before generating results.
- Use **Configure** to adjust report settings and **Filters** to narrow report results.
- The information displayed in a report depends on the selected period, grouping, filters, and recorded stock transactions.
- Always review the report settings before using the results for inventory reconciliation or business decisions.

docs/sales/add-credit-note.title: Add Credit Note
docs/sales/add-credit-note.description: Issue a credit note against previously sold drugs, select the customer, choose the items, and create the note in seconds.
docs/sales/add-credit-note.body: # Add Credit Note A **Credit Note** is issued when a customer returns medicines that were previously sold to them. Instead of manually adjusting the bill, MediFlux lets you select the exact drugs from the customer's sales history and generate a credit note against those items, keeping your records accurate and your inventory updated. Navigate here from the sidebar: **Sales → Add Credit Note**. ![Add Credit Note](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783673371852-466868674-creditnote-sidebar.png) *Caption: Navigate to Add Credit Note from sidebar.* --- ## How To Create A Credit Note 1. **Select the date and customer** At the top of the page, set the **date** for the credit note and search for the **customer** whose items are being returned. Once a customer is selected, their profile appears below the search bar showing their name and phone number. Their complete list of previously sold drugs loads automatically, showing **X items** in total. ![Customer selected](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783673562434-486678178-drug-selected.png) *Caption: Customer profile loaded with their complete drug sales history.* 2. **Select the drugs to return** The drug table shows every drug previously sold to this customer with the following columns: | Column | Description | | --- | --- | | **Drug** | Name of the drug | | **Expiry** | Expiry date of the batch. Shown in red if expired | | **Batch** | Batch number | | **Sold** | Quantity originally sold to the customer | | **Free** | Free units given at time of sale, if any | | **Rate** | Sale rate per unit | | **Disc%** | Discount applied at time of sale | | **CN Qty** | Quantity being returned in this credit note. Enter the number here | | **Returned** | Quantity already returned previously, if any | | **Sale** | Link icon to view the original sale entry | Tick the checkbox next to any drug to select it for the credit note. Once selected, enter the **CN Qty**, the number of units being returned. The **Disc%** field also becomes editable if you need to adjust it. You can search within the drug list using the **Search in sold drugs** bar, or use the **All** dropdown to filter by drug type. ![Drug selected for return](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783673814119-396692688-columns.png) *Caption: CN Qty entered with summary bar showing live totals.* 3. **Review the summary and create** As you select drugs, the summary bar at the bottom updates live: **Items · After Disc + Tax = Total** Once you're happy with the selection, click **+ Create Credit Note** to finalise. Click **Clear** at the top-right to reset the entire form and start over. --- ## The Credit Note Invoice Once you click **+ Create Credit Note**, a credit note invoice is generated automatically showing: - Your store name, address, GSTIN, and DL number - Credit Note number (e.g. `CN/2026001`) and date - Customer name and phone number - Payment status as **Credited** - Full line item breakdown: Item, HSN, Batch, Expiry, Qty, Free, Rate, MRP, Discount, Tax, Total - Summary: Sub Total, Discount, CGST+SGST, Net Amount, and current Outstanding balance ![Credit Note invoice](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783673960073-253465354-customer-invoice.png ) *Caption: Generated credit note showing store details, line items, and summary.* Once created, this credit note is saved and can be viewed anytime from the customer's Billing Notes. --- ## After Creating A Credit Note * [Customer Ledger](/docs/customers/customer-ledger) - Verify the credit note reduced the customer's outstanding balance. * [Billing Notes](/docs/customers/billing-notes) - View the generated credit note invoice and print or share it. * [Drug List](/docs/inventory/drug-list) - Check that returned stock was added back to inventory. * [Sales List](/docs/sales/sale-list) - View the original sale alongside the credit note for complete history.

docs/sales/add-sale-retail.title: Add Retail Sale
docs/sales/add-sale-retail.description: Learn how to create a retail pharmacy bill in MediFlux. Add customers, scan prescriptions, manage payments, and adjust returns quickly.
docs/sales/add-sale-retail.body:
# Add Retail Sale

The **Add Sale** page is where you **create retail pharmacy bills** for individual customers, walk-in patients, and prescription-based sales in **MediFlux**. It is designed for fast, accurate billing with fields tailored to retail pharmacy workflows.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Sales → Add Sale**. You can also click the **`+` button** on any screen and select **Add Sale**, which opens in Retail mode by default.

![MediFlux Add Retail Sale Page](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935731862-717775708-add-retail-sale-sidebar.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux retail sale page showing customer lookup, drug table, and payment options for fast pharmacy billing.*

---

## Sale Modes

At the top-right of the Add Sale page, you can switch between two modes:

| Mode | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **Retail** | Bills for individual customers, walk-in patients, and prescription-based sales |
| **Wholesale** | Bulk sale bills for other pharmacies and businesses |

---

## Scan & Add Drugs

Click **Scan** at the top-right to open the **Scan & Add Drugs** panel. This is designed for **phones and tablets** and opens your device camera for two input methods:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Barcode Scanner** | Scan drug barcodes with your phone or tablet camera to instantly add items to the bill |
| **Image (OCR)** | Photograph a prescription, drug label, or drug list with your camera. MediFlux reads the text and populates drugs automatically |

Camera permissions are required for both options on phones and tablets.

![MediFlux Barcode Scanner and OCR Prescription Scan](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/154fd3cb-3d9d-4e55-a0f3-778a8db3aa1f-scan-retail-sale.png)
*Caption: Use the MediFlux barcode scanner or OCR image scan to quickly add drugs to a retail pharmacy bill.*

If you have a **physical barcode scanner device** connected to your computer, you can scan barcodes directly into the bill without opening the Scan panel.

The drug is added instantly with auto-populated name, batch, expiry, MRP, and available stock.

> **[Note]** For detailed setup instructions, supported devices, OCR best practices, and troubleshooting, see the [Scan & OCR](/docs/sales/scan-and-ocr) guide.

---

## Drafts

Click **Drafts** at the top-right to access all saved draft bills. Any bill you save midway using **Save Draft** is stored here and can be resumed at any time.

If you are in the middle of adding a sale and need to navigate away, click **Save Draft** to save your progress. You can return to it anytime from Drafts.

![MediFlux Saved Draft Bills Panel](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935770855-591226455-retail-drafts.png)
*Caption: Access and resume saved draft pharmacy bills anytime in MediFlux.*

---

## Retail Sale

The **Retail** mode is designed for fast, accurate billing with fields tailored to retail pharmacy workflows, customer lookup, doctor details, prescription uploads, and MRP-based pricing.

### Left Panel

The left panel in Retail mode has three options:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Add Customer** `Ctrl+C` | Search for an existing customer or quickly add a new one. Shows **Currently Cash Sale** when no customer is selected |
| **Stock Issue Bill** | Switch to a Stock Issue bill for internal inventory reduction |
| **Local Sale (CGST/SGST)** | Toggle between Local Sale (CGST+SGST tax) and Out of State (IGST tax) |

![MediFlux Retail Sale Left Panel Options](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935818505-509551752-add-customer.png)
*Caption: The left panel in MediFlux retail sale showing Add Customer, Stock Issue Bill, and Local Sale tax toggle.*

#### Adding a Customer

Click **Add Customer** or press `Ctrl+C` to open the **Quick Add Customer** dialog. Search for an existing customer by name, phone, or Aadhaar number.

If the customer doesn't exist, press `Tab` or `Enter` to open a quick registration form:

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Name** | Yes | Customer's full name |
| **Phone** | Yes | Contact number |
| **Address** | Yes | Customer's address |
| **State** | Yes | Customer's state |
| **Gender** | No | M / F / O |
| **Age** | No | Customer's age |
| **Aadhaar** | No | 12-digit Aadhaar number |
| **PMJAY / Ayushman Bharat Customer** | No | Tick if this is a PMJAY beneficiary |

Click **Save Customer** to create the profile and link them to the sale instantly.

![MediFlux Quick Add Customer Dialog](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935818504-697694370-add-customer-dialog.png)
*Caption: Search existing pharmacy customers or register a new consumer or business profile on the fly during billing.*

> **[Note]** For full details on customer management, see [Add a Customer](/docs/customers/add-customer).

---

### Doctor Details

The right panel in Retail mode shows fields for recording prescription information:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Doctor who prescribed** | Name of the prescribing doctor |
| **Doctor License No** | Doctor's license number |
| **OPD / Case Number** | OPD or case number for this prescription |

![MediFlux Doctor Details for Prescription Sales](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935868199-981150094-doctor-details.png)
*Caption: Record the prescribing doctor's name, license number, and OPD case number for pharmacy prescription sales.*

These fields are optional but recommended for prescription-based sales and audit trails.

---

### Payment Status

Select the payment status for this sale:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Paid** | Full payment received |
| **Unpaid** | No payment received yet |
| **Partial** | Partial payment received |

When **Paid** or **Partial** is selected, additional fields appear:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Payment Method** | Cash, Card, UPI, or Net Banking |
| **Paid Amount** | Amount received |
| **Discount %** | Overall discount on the bill |

When **Cash** is selected as the payment method, no additional bank details are needed.

![MediFlux Payment Status and Method Selection](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935868198-365651859-payment-methods.png)
*Caption: Select Paid, Unpaid, or Partial payment status with payment method and linked bank account details in MediFlux.*

When **Card**, **UPI**, or **Net Banking** is selected, a **bank details dropdown** appears below showing your linked accounts. Select the appropriate account to record where the payment was received.

When **Unpaid** is selected, the Payment Method defaults to **None**, Paid Amount and Discount % remain editable, and the bank details section is hidden.

---

## Adjusted Returns

**Adjusted Returns** lets you adjust a customer's return amount against a new or existing sale.

You can use this feature while **adding a new sale** or **editing an existing sale**.

Adjusted Returns are supported in:

- **Retail Sale**, when a customer is selected
- **Wholesale Sale**
- **Challan Sale**

> **[Warning: Customer selection is required]** Adjusted Returns cannot be used for walk-in customers. You must select a customer before applying a return adjustment.

### Ways to Adjust a Return

There are two ways to adjust returns:

| Method | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| **Direct Return** | Enter a return amount in the **Direct Return (₹)** field |
| **Medicine Return** | Select the **Rtn** checkbox beside individual medicines in the sale table |

Use **Direct Return** when you want to enter the return amount directly. Use **Rtn** when you want to return specific medicines.

### Method 1: Direct Return

The **Direct Return (₹)** field appears in the payment section of the sale form.

This field allows you to enter an amount that should be adjusted against the current sale bill.

#### How to Apply a Direct Return

1. **Select a customer**

   Go to **Sales → Add Sale** or open an existing sale for editing.

   Select the customer whose return amount you want to adjust.

   The **Direct Return (₹)** field is unavailable when no customer is selected.

   ![MediFlux Direct Return Disabled for Walk-in Sales](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/87be4e98-f12f-4668-947d-a828a04ed5bb-direct-return.png)
*Caption: The Direct Return field is disabled in MediFlux when no specific customer is selected for the pharmacy sale.*

2. **Add medicines**

   Enter the medicines being sold, including quantities and prices.

3. **Enter the return amount**

   Locate **Direct Return (₹)** in the payment section.

   Enter the amount to adjust.

   For example, enter `1500` to adjust ₹1,500 against the current bill.

   ![MediFlux Direct Return Adjustment Example](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/0bcd1aa5-2f6e-4df6-977f-60adecbe3e25-direct-return-sale-eg.png)
*Caption: A ₹1,500 direct return adjustment reduces the gross pharmacy sale amount of ₹2,276 to a net bill of ₹776.*

4. **Review the adjusted bill**

   MediFlux deducts the return amount from the gross sale total.

   The bottom summary bar updates to show the return adjustment and remaining net bill.

5. **Choose the payment status**

   Select **Paid**, **Partial**, or **Unpaid**, depending on how the remaining amount will be settled.

6. **Save the sale**

   Click **Add** to create the sale or **Update** when editing an existing sale.

---

### How Direct Return Affects the Sale Amount

The result depends on whether the return amount is equal to, less than, or greater than the sale amount.

#### Case 1: Return Amount Equals the Sale Amount

When the return amount equals the gross sale amount, the entire bill is adjusted against the return.

For example:

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Amount | ₹2,276 |
| Direct Return | -₹2,276 |
| Net Payable | ₹0 |

The sale is marked as **Paid by Cash**, with no remaining amount to collect.

---

#### Case 2: Return Amount Is Less Than the Sale Amount

When the return amount is less than the gross sale amount, the return is adjusted first.

The remaining balance is handled according to the selected payment status.

For example:

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Amount | ₹2,276 |
| Direct Return | -₹1,500 |
| Remaining Amount | ₹776 |

![MediFlux Return Amount Less Than Sale Amount](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/0bcd1aa5-2f6e-4df6-977f-60adecbe3e25-direct-return-sale-eg.png)
*Caption: A gross pharmacy bill of ₹2,276 is reduced by a ₹1,500 direct return, leaving ₹776 payable in MediFlux.*

You can handle the remaining ₹776 in three ways:

| Payment Status | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Paid** | The remaining ₹776 is recorded as paid by cash |
| **Partial** | The entered Paid Amount is deducted from ₹776, and the rest is recorded as customer credit |
| **Unpaid** | The entire remaining ₹776 is recorded as customer credit |

##### Example: Paid Sale

If you select **Paid**, the remaining ₹776 is recorded as paid by cash.

The sale is completed without an outstanding balance from this bill.

##### Example: Partial Sale

Suppose the customer pays ₹200 after the return adjustment.

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Amount | ₹2,276 |
| Direct Return | -₹1,500 |
| Remaining Amount | ₹776 |
| Paid Amount | -₹200 |
| Outstanding Credit | ₹576 |

The remaining ₹576 is recorded in the customer's ledger.

##### Example: Unpaid Sale

If you select **Unpaid**, the entire remaining ₹776 is recorded as credit against the customer's account.

You can review the outstanding balance in [Customer Ledger](/docs/customers/customer-ledger).

> **[Note]** The return amount is adjusted against the sale first. Any remaining amount is then handled according to the selected payment status.

---

#### Case 3: Return Amount Exceeds the Sale Amount

When the return amount exceeds the gross sale amount, MediFlux displays the **Return Amount Exceeds Sale Bill** dialog.

The dialog shows:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Gross Sale Total** | Total value of the current sale |
| **Return Total** | Total return amount being adjusted |
| **Excess Balance Owed** | Amount remaining after adjusting the entire sale |

For example:

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Total | ₹2,276 |
| Return Total | -₹2,500 |
| Excess Balance Owed | ₹224 |

The full ₹2,276 sale is adjusted, and ₹224 remains owed to the customer.

You must choose how to handle the excess ₹224 before completing the sale.

##### Option 1: Keep as Credit

Select **Keep as Credit** to retain the excess amount in the customer's account.

The amount is saved as advance credit for future purchases and reduces the customer's outstanding balance.

![MediFlux Keep Excess Return as Customer Credit](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/f5e7f60c-edb3-4e85-b08b-c0f0e526cbe5-keep-as-credit.png)
*Caption: Choose Keep as Credit in MediFlux to retain an excess pharmacy return amount in the customer's account for future purchases.*

Click **Confirm & Complete Sale** to save the adjustment.

##### Option 2: Refund to Customer

Select **Refund to Customer** to pay the excess amount back to the customer.

The dialog provides the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Refund Amount (₹)** | Amount to refund, which can be edited |
| **Payment Method** | Select the refund method, such as Cash, Card, or UPI |
| **Receipt / Transaction Ref** | Optional reference number for the refund |

1. **Select Refund to Customer**

   In the **Return Amount Exceeds Sale Bill** dialog, choose **Refund to Customer**.

2. **Review the refund amount**

   The excess balance appears in **Refund Amount (₹)**.

   In this example, the excess balance is ₹224.

   Edit the amount if required.

3. **Choose the payment method**

   Select the method used to refund the customer.

4. **Enter a reference if needed**

   Optionally enter a receipt or transaction reference.

5. **Complete the sale**

   Click **Confirm & Complete Sale** to record the sale and refund adjustment.

![MediFlux Refund Excess Return to Customer](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/5272327b-baa4-4fe1-9b50-6da7847c9407-refund-to-customer.png)
*Caption: Enter the refund amount, choose a payment method, and provide a transaction reference for excess pharmacy returns in MediFlux.*

> **[Note]** When the return amount exceeds the sale amount, MediFlux asks whether to retain the excess as customer credit or refund it to the customer.

---

### Method 2: Return Individual Medicines Using Rtn

You can also adjust returns by selecting specific medicines in the sale table.

The **Rtn** column contains a checkbox beside each medicine row.

Select this checkbox for the medicines being returned.

#### How to Return Individual Medicines

1. **Select a customer**

   Open **Add Sale** or **Edit Sale** and select the customer.

2. **Locate the medicines**

   In the drug table, find the medicines you want to return.

3. **Select Rtn**

   Tick the checkbox under **Rtn** beside each medicine being returned.

4. **Review the sale**

   Review the return adjustment and updated bill totals.

5. **Save the sale**

   Click **Add** or **Update** to complete the sale.

> **[Note]** Use **Direct Return** to enter a return amount manually. Use **Rtn** to select individual medicines for return.

---

### Viewing Adjusted Returns in the Sale Summary

After applying a return, the sale summary displays the adjustment alongside the bill totals.

For example:

| Summary Field | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| **Subtotal** | ₹2,275.64 |
| **Total Discount** | ₹0 |
| **Total Tax** | ₹0 |
| **Gross Total** | ₹2,276 |
| **Direct Return Amount** | ₹1,500 |
| **Return Adjustment** | -₹1,500 |
| **Net Payable** | ₹776 |

The bottom summary bar also shows the return adjustment and remaining net bill.

![MediFlux Adjusted Return Calculation Breakdown](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/0bcd1aa5-2f6e-4df6-977f-60adecbe3e25-direct-return-sale-eg.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux summary shows ₹2,275.64 subtotal, ₹2,276 rounded gross total, ₹1,500 return adjustment, and ₹776 net payable.*

### Adjusted Returns in Sale Confirmation

When the sale is successfully recorded, the **Sale Recorded!** dialog displays the sale details and indicates that a return adjustment was applied.

For example:

`Return Adjusted: -₹1500.00`

The dialog also provides the usual options to view, print, or share the invoice.

![MediFlux Sale Recorded with Adjusted Return](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/b232a132-4e68-4e3c-9cc2-8c8f0c878c90-adjusted-sale.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux confirmation dialog shows that a return adjustment was successfully applied to the pharmacy sale.*

---

### Adjusted Returns While Editing a Sale

Adjusted Returns are also supported when editing an existing sale.

The **Edit Sale** page provides the same **Direct Return (₹)** field and **Rtn** checkboxes for individual medicines.

You can modify the return adjustment and review the updated totals before saving.

1. **Open the sale for editing**

   Open the existing sale in **Edit Sale**.

2. **Update the return**

   Enter or modify the **Direct Return (₹)** amount, or use **Rtn** to mark individual medicines for return.

3. **Review payment details**

   Check the updated net bill and choose the appropriate payment status.

   For example, with a ₹776 net bill, a ₹200 partial payment leaves ₹576 outstanding.

4. **Save the changes**

   Click **Update** to save the edited sale.

---

### Important Points About Adjusted Returns

- A customer must be selected before using Adjusted Returns.
- Adjusted Returns are not available for walk-in customers.
- You can use **Direct Return** or select individual medicines through **Rtn**.
- Returns can be adjusted while adding or editing a sale.
- If the return equals the sale amount, the sale is marked as paid by cash.
- If the return is less than the sale amount, the remaining amount follows the selected payment status.
- If the return exceeds the sale amount, the excess can be retained as customer credit or refunded.
- Unpaid amounts can be reviewed in the customer's ledger.

---

### Drug Table

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **S.No** | Serial number |
| **Rtn** | Select the checkbox to mark an individual medicine for return |
| **Type** | Drug type: Rx, NRx, H1 |
| **Drug** | Drug name |
| **Batch** | Batch number |
| **Expiry** | Expiry date |
| **QTY** | Quantity sold |
| **TABS** | Number of tablets/units |
| **MRP** | Maximum Retail Price |
| **DISC%** | Discount percentage |
| **Total** | Line item total |

Click the **grid icon (⊞)** at the bottom of the table to add more drug rows.

![MediFlux Pharmacy Drug Table in Retail Sale](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935922683-888144517-medicine-grid.png)
*Caption: Add drugs to the MediFlux retail sale with batch, expiry, quantity, MRP, discount, and individual return (Rtn) selection.*

---

### Quick Add Drug (Alt + D)

If a medicine is not available in your Drug List while creating a sale, you can add it directly without leaving the **Add Sale** page.

Press `Alt + D` to open the **Quick Add Drug** dialog. The medicine name you were searching for is automatically filled in, so you do not need to type it again.

![MediFlux Quick Add Drug from Billing Screen](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/5284e8b8-733f-40a2-9229-a47eb19c6713-quick-add-drug.png)
*Caption: Add a new medicine directly from the MediFlux Add Sale page using Alt + D without interrupting the pharmacy billing process.*

#### How To Quickly Add A Drug

1. **Search for a medicine**

   On the **Add Sale** page, start typing the medicine name in the **Drug** field.

   If the medicine is not available in your inventory, press `Alt + D`.

   The **Quick Add Drug** dialog opens with the searched medicine name already filled in.

2. **Enter medicine details**

   Complete the required medicine information.

   | Field | Description |
   | --- | --- |
   | **Name** | Medicine name, prefilled from your search |
   | **Cost Price (₹)** | Purchase cost of the medicine |
   | **Unit Cost (₹)** | Cost per individual unit |
   | **MRP (₹)** | Maximum Retail Price |
   | **HSN Code** | HSN code for the medicine |
   | **Batch Number** | Medicine batch number, optional |
   | **Opening Stock** | Initial stock quantity |
   | **Expiry Date** | Expiry in `MM YY` format |
   | **Units Per Pack** | Number of units in each pack |
   | **Rack Number** | Storage rack or shelf location, optional |
   | **CGST (%)** | Central GST rate |
   | **SGST (%)** | State GST rate |
   | **IGST (%)** | Integrated GST rate |
   | **Dosage Form** | Medicine form, such as Tablet |
   | **Classification** | Medicine category, such as Rx |

   Fields marked with `*` are required.

3. **Save the medicine**

   Review the entered details and click **Save Drug**.

   The medicine is added to your inventory and becomes available for the current sale without requiring you to leave the billing page.

   Continue entering the remaining sale details as usual.

> **[Note]** The `Alt + D` shortcut is useful when billing a medicine that has not yet been added to your Drug List. You can create its inventory entry and continue the same sale without navigating to a separate page.

---

### Additional Notes

Both Retail and Wholesale forms have an **Additional Notes** field for entering specific instructions, clinical notes, or delivery remarks.

![MediFlux Additional Notes for Pharmacy Sales](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935922678-913599840-additional-notes.png)
*Caption: Enter clinical notes, delivery remarks, or specific instructions for a pharmacy sale in MediFlux.*

---

### Prescription Management & Documents

If the customer has a physical prescription, you can upload it directly instead of manually entering each drug line by line. MediFlux will scan the prescription and fill in the drug details automatically, saving you time and reducing manual errors.

Click **+ Upload Prescription** to attach a scanned or photographed prescription. Once uploaded, the drugs from the prescription are read and added to the bill automatically.

You can also attach any additional supporting documents, reports, referral letters, or delivery notes using **+ Add More Files**.

![MediFlux Prescription Upload and OCR Scan](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783935922677-222683802-upload-prescription.png)
*Caption: Upload physical prescriptions in MediFlux for automatic drug population and faster pharmacy billing via OCR.*

---

### Bill Summary Bar

At the bottom of the page, a fixed summary bar shows a live breakdown of the bill:

**Sub Total − Disc + Tax = Bill**

When an adjusted return is applied, the summary also shows the return deduction and the remaining net bill.

For example:

**₹2,276 Gross − ₹1,500 Return = ₹776 Net Bill**

---

### Saving and Submitting

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Save Draft** | Saves the bill as a draft so you can resume it later from Drafts |
| **+ Add** | Finalises and saves the sale bill |
| **Update** | Saves changes when editing an existing sale |

---

## Wholesale Sale

The **Wholesale** mode is for bulk sale bills to other pharmacies and businesses. Switch to Wholesale using the toggle at the top-right.

Adjusted Returns are also supported in Wholesale Sale.

For full details on bulk pricing and business customer fields, see [Add Wholesale Sale](/docs/sales/add-wholesale).

---

## After The Sale


  * [Sales List](/docs/sales/sale-list) - View, print, or share the invoice you just created.
  * [Customer Ledger](/docs/customers/customer-ledger) - Verify payment was recorded and check outstanding balance.
  * [Customer Profile](/docs/customers/customer-profile) - View this customer's full purchase history.
  * [Add Credit Note](/docs/sales/add-credit-note) - Correct the bill if you made an error.

docs/sales/add-wholesale.title: Add Wholesale
docs/sales/add-wholesale.description: Learn how to create a wholesale pharmacy bill or Challan in MediFlux. Manage HSN codes, split taxes, adjusted returns, and bulk pricing easily.
docs/sales/add-wholesale.body:
# Add Wholesale

The **Add Wholesale** page is where you **create wholesale pharmacy bills** and Challans for other pharmacies, distributors, and businesses in **MediFlux**. It supports both normal sale invoicing and **Challan mode** for delivery notes that can be converted to sales later. The wholesale layout includes additional columns for HSN codes, free units, discounts, and split tax breakdowns.

Navigate here from the sidebar: **Sales → Add Sale**, then click **Wholesale** at the top-right.

![MediFlux Add Wholesale Pharmacy Sale Page](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783937800722-967118673-add-sale-sidebar.png)
*Caption: The MediFlux wholesale sale page showing Challan toggle, customer selection, and the wholesale drug table.*

---

## Scan & Add Drugs

Click **Scan** at the top-right to open the **Scan & Add Drugs** panel. This is designed for **phones and tablets** and opens your device camera for two input methods:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Barcode Scanner** | Scan drug barcodes with your phone or tablet camera to instantly add items to the bill |
| **Image (OCR)** | Photograph a prescription, drug label, or drug list with your camera. MediFlux reads the text and populates drugs automatically |

Camera permissions are required for both options on phones and tablets.

If you have a **physical barcode scanner device** connected to your computer, you can scan barcodes directly into the bill without opening the Scan panel. The drug is added instantly with auto-populated name, batch, expiry, MRP, and available stock.

> **[Note]** For detailed setup instructions, supported devices, OCR best practices, and troubleshooting, see the [Scan & OCR](/docs/sales/scan-and-ocr) guide.

---

## Drafts

Click **Drafts** at the top-right to access all saved draft bills. Any bill you save midway using **Save Draft** is stored here and can be resumed at any time.

If you are in the middle of adding a sale and need to navigate away, click **Save Draft** to save your progress. You can return to it anytime from Drafts.

![MediFlux Saved Wholesale Draft Bills Panel](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783937800716-13436338-wholesale-draft.png)
*Caption: Access and resume saved draft wholesale pharmacy bills anytime in MediFlux.*

---

## Left Panel

The left panel in Wholesale mode has two options:

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Sale Mode** `Shift+S` | Toggle between normal sale mode and Challan mode |
| **Local Sale (CGST/SGST)** | Toggle between Local Sale (CGST+SGST tax) and Out of State (IGST tax) |

![MediFlux Wholesale Sale Mode and Tax Toggle](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783937800715-605577947-sale-mode.png)
*Caption: The left panel in MediFlux wholesale sale showing the Sale Mode toggle and Local Sale tax switch.*

### Sale Mode: Normal vs Challan

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Sale Mode** | Creates a standard wholesale invoice with full payment tracking |
| **Challan Mode** | Creates a delivery challan without immediate payment. The challan is saved as a pending delivery note and can be converted into a sale later |

Challan mode is useful when goods are dispatched before payment terms are finalised or when the exact invoice details need to be confirmed after delivery.

Once converted to a sale, the challan becomes a regular wholesale bill with payment status tracking.

---

## Customer and Salesperson

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Customer Details** | Search and select the customer for this wholesale sale |
| **Select Salesperson** *(Optional)* | Assign a salesperson to this sale for tracking commissions and performance reporting |

![MediFlux Wholesale Customer and Salesperson Selection](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783938063319-96447838-customer-salesperson.png)
*Caption: Select a wholesale pharmacy customer and assign a salesperson for commission tracking in MediFlux.*

---

## Payment Status

Select the payment status for this sale:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Paid** | Full payment received |
| **Unpaid** | No payment received yet |
| **Partial** | Partial payment received |

![MediFlux Wholesale Payment Status Options](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783938063317-807345784-payment-options.png)
*Caption: Choose between Paid, Unpaid, or Partial payment status for wholesale pharmacy bills.*

When **Paid** or **Partial** is selected, additional fields appear:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Payment Method** | Cash, Card, UPI, or Net Banking |
| **Paid Amount** | Amount received |
| **Discount %** | Overall discount on the bill |

When **Cash** is selected as the payment method, no additional bank details are needed.

When **Card**, **UPI**, or **Net Banking** is selected, a **bank details dropdown** appears below showing your linked accounts. Select the appropriate account to record where the payment was received.

![MediFlux Linked Bank Account Details for Wholesale](https://waibusiness.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/media/1783938135349-539772848-bank-details.png)
*Caption: Select the linked bank account for Card, UPI, or Net Banking payments in MediFlux wholesale sales.*

When **Unpaid** is selected, the Payment Method defaults to **None**, Paid Amount and Discount % remain editable, and the bank details section is hidden.

---

## Adjusted Returns

**Adjusted Returns** allows you to adjust a customer's return amount against a new or existing wholesale sale or challan.

You can apply the adjustment while **adding a sale** or **editing an existing sale**.

There are two ways to adjust returns:

| Method | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| **Direct Return** | Enter a return amount directly in **Direct Return (₹)** |
| **Medicine Return** | Select **Rtn** beside individual medicines in the drug table |

> **[Note]** Adjusted Returns are available in **Wholesale Sale** and **Challan Mode**. You can also use the feature in Retail Sale when a customer is selected.

### Method 1: Direct Return

Use **Direct Return** when you want to adjust a return amount against the current bill without selecting individual medicines.

#### How to Apply a Direct Return

1. **Select a customer**

   Open **Sales → Add Sale**, switch to **Wholesale**, and select the customer.

   You can also open an existing wholesale sale for editing.

2. **Add medicines**

   Enter the medicines being sold, along with their quantities, rates, and applicable discounts.

3. **Enter the return amount**

   Locate **Direct Return (₹)** in the payment section.

   Enter the amount you want to adjust against the sale.

   For example, enter `1500` to adjust ₹1,500 against the current bill.

   ![MediFlux Direct Return Adjustment in Wholesale Billing](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/da1320d8-b064-4215-8f9a-1a6de563a5bf-adjusted-return-wholesale.png)
*Caption: Enter a return amount to adjust it against the current wholesale pharmacy sale in MediFlux.*

4. **Review the updated total**

   MediFlux deducts the return amount from the gross sale total.

   The bill summary updates to show the return adjustment and remaining amount.

5. **Choose the payment status**

   If an amount remains payable, select **Paid**, **Partial**, or **Unpaid** as appropriate.

6. **Complete the sale**

   Click **+ Add** to save the new sale or **Update** when editing an existing sale.

---

### How Direct Return Affects Payment

The adjustment depends on whether the return amount is equal to, less than, or greater than the sale amount.

#### Case 1: Return Amount Equals the Sale Amount

When the return amount equals the gross sale amount, the entire bill is adjusted against the return.

For example:

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Amount | ₹1,500 |
| Direct Return | -₹1,500 |
| Net Payable | ₹0 |

The sale is marked as **Paid by Cash**, with no remaining amount to collect.

---

#### Case 2: Return Amount Is Less Than the Sale Amount

When the return amount is less than the gross sale amount, MediFlux adjusts the return first.

For example:

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Amount | ₹2,435 |
| Direct Return | -₹1,500 |
| Remaining Amount | ₹935 |

The remaining ₹935 is handled according to the payment status:

| Payment Status | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Paid** | The remaining amount is recorded as paid by cash |
| **Partial** | The entered payment is deducted from the remaining amount, and the rest is recorded as customer credit |
| **Unpaid** | The entire remaining amount is recorded as customer credit |

##### Example: Partial Payment

Suppose the customer pays ₹200 after the return adjustment.

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Amount | ₹2,230 |
| Direct Return | -₹1,500 |
| Remaining Amount | ₹730 |
| Paid Amount | -₹200 |
| Outstanding Credit | ₹530 |

The remaining ₹530 is recorded as outstanding credit.

![MediFlux Wholesale Direct Return with Partial Payment](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/610538f0-57e7-4268-b209-45b5d05cd5f4-directreturn-partial-payment.png)
*Caption: The return is deducted from the wholesale sale first, and the unpaid portion is recorded as customer credit in MediFlux.*

You can review the outstanding balance in [Customer Ledger](/docs/customers/customer-ledger).

> **[Note]** The return amount is adjusted first. Any remaining amount is then handled according to the selected payment status.

---

#### Case 3: Return Amount Exceeds the Sale Amount

When the return amount exceeds the gross sale amount, MediFlux displays the **Return Amount Exceeds Sale Bill** dialog.

The dialog shows:

- **Gross Sale Total**
- **Return Total**
- **Excess Balance Owed**

For example:

| Description | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Gross Sale Total | ₹1,826 |
| Return Total | -₹2,000 |
| Excess Balance Owed | ₹174 |

You must choose how to handle the excess amount.

##### Option 1: Keep as Credit

Select **Keep as Credit** to retain the excess amount in the customer's account.

The excess is saved as advance credit for future purchases and reduces the customer's outstanding balance.

![MediFlux Keep Excess Wholesale Return as Customer Credit](https://pub-edab995818924e31a696b8a8c0fd961b.r2.dev/mediflux-docs/2026/10/d4b19b77-52c4-4d43-8bf3-a1d96177d045-wholesale-keepcredit.png)
*Caption: Retain the excess wholesale return amount as customer credit instead of issuing a refund in MediFlux.*

Click **Confirm & Complete Sale** to save the adjustment.

##### Option 2: Refund to Customer

Select **Refund to Customer** to return the excess amount to the customer.

The dialog provides:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Refund Amount (₹)** | Amount to refund, which can be edited |
| **Payment Method** | Cash, Card, UPI, or another available method |
| **Receipt / Transaction Ref** | Optional reference number for the refund |

1. **Select Refund to Customer**

   Choose **Refund to Customer** in the excess-return dialog.

2. **Enter the refund amount**

   Review or edit the amount shown in **Refund Amount (₹)**.

3. **Select a payment method**

   Choose the method used to refund the customer.

4. **Enter a reference if needed**
