help/sales/draft-and-add-sale-diff.title: What is the difference between Save Draft and Add on a sale?
help/sales/draft-and-add-sale-diff.description: Understand why saving a sale as a draft does not add it as a completed sale.
help/sales/draft-and-add-sale-diff.body:
# What is the difference between Save Draft and Add on a sale?

**Save Draft does not add the sale.** It only saves the sale so you can come back and complete it later.

A sale is added only when you complete the sale and select **+ Add**. Until then, the sale remains under **Sales → Drafts** and is not treated as a completed sale.

Use **Save Draft** when you need to pause the billing process, review the details later, or complete the sale at another time. When you are ready to finalise it, open the draft and select **+ Add**.

Both actions appear in the billing footer: **Save Draft** stores the current bill under **Sales → Drafts** without deducting inventory, while **+ Add** finalises the transaction and commits the sale.

> **[Note]** A saved draft is not a completed sale. Saving it does not add the sale to your sales records.

## Related

* [Drafts](/docs/sales/drafts.md)

help/sales/nrx-sale.title: How do I make an NRx or H1 sale?
help/sales/nrx-sale.description: Sell non-prescription (NRx) or Schedule H1 drugs using the normal Add Sale flow. The drug Type is set automatically.
help/sales/nrx-sale.body:
# How do I make an NRx or H1 sale?

NRx and H1 sales use the same **Add Sale** flow as a regular retail sale. The drug **Type** (`NRx` or `H1`) is set automatically from the drug master.

---

## Steps

1. Go to **Sales → Add Sale** (or use the **+** button and select **Add Sale**).
2. Add the customer if needed.
3. Search or scan the drug and add it to the bill.
4. Check the **Type** column in the drug table. It will show `NRx` or `H1` based on how the drug is configured.
5. Complete payment details and click **+ Add** to finalise the sale.

![Drug Type column](/images/faqs/nrx-h1-type-column.png)
*Caption: Type column in the Add Sale drug table showing Rx, NRx, or H1.*

---

> **[Note]** Make sure the drug is correctly marked as NRx or H1 in the drug master. If the Type is wrong, update the drug profile first.

## Related

* [Sales](/docs/sales)

help/sales/print-or-share-bill.title: How do I print or share a bill?
help/sales/print-or-share-bill.description: Print, download, or share a completed sale invoice from MediFlux.
help/sales/print-or-share-bill.body:
# How do I print or share a bill?

You can print or download a bill by opening its invoice from **Sales → Sales List**.

1. **Open the invoice**

   Find the sale you want to print or share. Select the three-dot menu (⋮) and choose **View Invoice**.

2. **Print or download the bill**

   In the invoice dialog, choose the required action:

   - **Print**: Print the invoice.
   - **Thermal**: Print the invoice using a thermal printer.
   - **Download**: Download the invoice to your device.

## Related

help/sales/return-sale.title: How do I return a sale?
help/sales/return-sale.description: Return a completed sale from the Sales List and record any applicable refund.
help/sales/return-sale.body:
# How do I return a sale?

You can return a completed sale directly from **Sales → Sales List**.

1. **Select the sale**

   Find the sale you want to return and select the three-dot menu (⋮) on its row. Choose **Return Sale**.

2. **Enter return details**

   Review the customer name, sale number, and outstanding balance.

   Select whether a refund was initiated:

   - **Yes**: Enter the refund amount and, optionally, a receipt number.
   - **No**: Select this if no refund is being given.

3. **Confirm the return**

   Select **Return Sale** to confirm.

Click **Return Sale** to confirm the return (or **Cancel** to exit without changes); a **Sale returned successfully!** toast confirms the return, and the transaction is recorded under **Returned Sales**.

> **[Warning: Important]** Returning a sale cannot be undone. All drugs in the sale are added back to inventory immediately. Make sure the details are correct before confirming.

## Related

help/sales/todays-sale.title: How do I check today's sales?
help/sales/todays-sale.description: View recent sales and filter the Sales List to check today's sales.
help/sales/todays-sale.body:
# How do I check today's sales?

You can check today's sales directly from **Sales → Sales List**.

Recent sales are displayed by default, so you can immediately view the latest recorded sales without applying any filters.

To view only today's sales, select **Filter** and set the date to today's date. The Sales List will then display the sales recorded for the selected date.

You can review the sale details, customer information, invoice numbers, and payment details from the list.

# How do I edit a sale?

You can update an existing sale from **Sales → Sales List**.

help/sales/wrong-calculations.title: Why is the total wrong when I sell tablets instead of a full strip?
help/sales/wrong-calculations.description: Wrong bill totals when selling loose tablets usually mean Units were not set correctly at the time of purchase.
help/sales/wrong-calculations.body:
# Why is the total wrong when I sell tablets instead of a full strip?

When you sell loose tablets (for example 10 tablets from a strip of 20), the total is calculated from the unit price. If **Units** were not entered correctly when the stock was purchased, the calculation will be wrong.

---

## Why this happens

At the time of purchase, each item needs the correct **Units** value (tablets per strip / pack).

Example:
- Strip contains 20 tablets
- Purchase Qty = 1
- Units must be set to `20`

If Units is left as `1` or `0`, the system treats the whole strip price as the price of one tablet and the bill total becomes incorrect.

---

## How to fix it

### Option 1: Update the purchase (recommended if recent)

1. Go to the original purchase bill.
2. Edit the line for that drug.
3. Set the correct **Units** value (e.g. `20`).
4. Save the purchase.

### Option 2: Update from Drug List

1. Go to **Drugs → Drug List**.
2. Switch to **Separated View**.
3. Find the drug and batch.
4. Click **Edit** and enter the correct **Units**.
5. Save.

![Drug List – Separated View](/images/faqs/drug-list-separated-view.png)
*Caption: Separated View showing individual batches where you can edit Units.*

![Edit Units](/images/faqs/edit-units-on-drug.png)
*Caption: Edit the drug or batch and set the correct Units (tablets per strip).*

After Units are corrected, new sales of loose tablets will calculate the unit price correctly.

---

## Quick check while billing

In the **Add Sale** drug table:

- **QTY** = number of strips / packs
- **TABS** = number of loose tablets

If you are selling only tablets, keep QTY at `0` (or blank) and enter the tablet count in **TABS**.

> **[IMAGE PENDING]** Example calculation demonstrating an incorrect bill total when TABS is entered without Units set at purchase. Source this image or expand this section with the specific data.

---

> **[Note]** Always set **Units** correctly when recording a purchase. This prevents wrong calculations later when selling loose tablets.
